body.text:
// slob dpon yon tan 'od gyis mdzad pa'i 'dul ba mdo ba'i lags so / shri la
a ka ras bris ga xiv.1 vinayasūtram guṇaprabha (62 patra)
Bhadantaguṇaprabhaviracitaṃ
[mūlasarvāstivādīyaṃ]
vinayasūtram /
body.translated_text:
// The <s>Vinayasūtra</s> composed by the teacher <s>Guṇaprabha</s>. Written by <s>Śrī Lakāra</s>. xiv.1 <s>Vinayasūtram</s> <s>Guṇaprabha</s> (62 folios)
Composed by the Venerable <s>Guṇaprabha</s>,
[belonging to the <s>Mūlasarvāstivāda</s> school],
the <s>Vinayasūtra</s>.

children.translated_text: <s>Vin</s> 1. The Chapter on Going Forth (<s>pravrajyāvastu</s>)
(<s>Vin</s> 1,1) The Procedure for Conferring <s>Śrāmaṇera</s> (Novice) Status
Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!
Now, the procedure of going forth (<s>niryāṇa</s>).

children.text: / sarvasmin* sannipatite saṃghe kṛtedaṃ veṣaṃ nipatya pragṛhītāñjalim utkuṭusthaṃ vṛddhāntaṃ yācivantaṃ trir jñapticaturthena karmaṇā saha pravrajyopasaṃpadāv upanayeyur iti purākalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the entire <s>Saṃgha</s> has assembled, one who has assumed this appearance, having prostrated, standing in a squatting posture with joined palms, ending with the elders, requesting — they should confer both going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>) and full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>) together by a motion followed by a fourth-act (<s>jñapticaturtha</s>) procedure — this is the ancient precedent.
For one who has taken dependence (<s>niśrita</s>), [there should be conferred] going forth and full ordination upon a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> serving as his preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>).
Having asked regarding impediments (<s>antarāyika</s>), for one who is pure, he should grant permission for the prior preceptorship.
The subsequent [conferral] of <s>upāsaka</s> (lay-follower), <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice), and <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) status should not [be given] to one who is unfit for the prior [stage].
Beginning with the words of acceptance of taking refuge, one should make the utterance of acceptance of <s>upāsaka</s> and <s>śrāmaṇera</s> status.
Immediately after, [there is] the proclamation of training rules for him, in the form of acceptance.
Having himself conferred <s>upāsaka</s> status, he should hand [the candidate] over to the announcing <s>bhikṣu</s> (<s>ārocaka</s>) for the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

children.text: / kañcit pariśuddhya tīti pṛṣṭvā śuddham ā[1b3]rocayet* /
children.translated_text: Having asked a certain [<s>bhikṣu</s>] 'Does he purify himself?', he should announce [him as] pure.
Either by an assembly of all, or, when [the <s>Saṃgha</s>] is seated, by going along [to each].
If all say 'He does purify himself.'
He should request a preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>).
He should have [his] hair and beard shaved, except for the topknot.
When asked 'Let the topknot be removed' and permission is given, [he should remove] it.
He should bathe.
The preceptor should give [him] saffron-dyed robes.
Having prostrated at [the preceptor's] feet, he should receive [them].
The preceptor should dress [him].
He should examine the [bodily] marks of one who has not been noticed [before].
He should confer going forth, beginning with the taking of refuge.
Or after the formal act (<s>yājñā</s>).
For one being conferred <s>śrāmaṇera</s> status, he should hand [him] over to the <s>bhikṣus</s>.
Having asked a certain [<s>bhikṣu</s>] 'Does he purify himself?', he should confer [status] upon the pure one.
He is the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher).
And [there should be appointed] a private instructor, act-performer, dependence-giver, and reciter.
The status of having been fulfilled [arises] when the matter is accomplished.
When the preceptor's formal act has been accepted, that [status] arises.
At the recurrence, in the third portion, at the end, the status of being fulfilled [is attained].
Namely, at the time of the other's proclamation — [the status] of <s>śrāmaṇera</s>-hood.
At the final [proclamation] — [the status] of preceptorship.
The limit of dependence-giving is one night of service as a dependent.
For recitation, the turning over of a single verse three times.
Utterance without the intention of teaching does not constitute recitation.
He should not confer [status] upon these two otherwise.
Nor in this way upon another.

children.text: / nānuktvā sahitam arthahetor nāma gṛhnāmīty upādhyāyanāma gṛhnīyāt*
children.translated_text: Without having said 'together, for the purpose of the meaning, I take the name,' he should take the preceptor's name.
// The procedure for conferring <s>śrāmaṇera</s> status //
(<s>Vin</s> 1,2) The Procedure for Full Ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>)
Full ordination [is obtained] from the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

children.text: / upādhyāyatāyām unmukhībhūtaḥ karmakārakam adhīcched raho nuśāsakañ ca bhikṣuṃ /
children.translated_text: One who has become inclined toward preceptorship should request a <s>bhikṣu</s> as act-performer and private instructor.
He should request a preceptor.
He (<s>the preceptor</s>) himself should have him don the three robes (<s>tricīvara</s>).

children.text: / pātrañ copadarśya monam a[2a1] / /dhikaṃ pāṇḍapetīti saṃghe /
children.translated_text: And having shown the bowl — 'silence; this is an additional begging vessel' — [thus he announces] to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
'It is a proper bowl' — thus all should say, not otherwise.

children.text: / apakasite ka ity ākhyāpya raha nuśāsakam utsāhya karmakārakaḥ saṃghaṃ yenam anujñā..payet* /
children.translated_text: When [the candidate] is set aside, having announced his identity, encouraging the private instructor, the act-performer should have the <s>Saṃgha</s> grant permission to him.
'Listen, you!' — thus he should instruct privately.

children.text: / tiṣṭha mā śabditā gamiṣyasīty enam uktvā samanuśiṣṭa iti saṃghāya pariśuddhiṃ nivedya kim āgacchatv ity āgamanaṃ pṛcchet* /
children.translated_text: Having said to him 'Stand; do not make noise; you will go,' having announced to the <s>Saṃgha</s> that he has been privately instructed, and having reported his purity, he should ask whether he may come: 'Shall he come?'
If all say 'He does purify himself,'
the act-performer should have [the candidate] request full ordination.
Having made the motion (<s>jñapti</s>), he should ask about impediments before the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
He should confer full ordination.
He should announce the shadow-[measurement], precisely measured, immediately after.
By a gnomon of four finger-breadths — this is correct.
The subsequent conduct toward him [is] as toward a [full] person.
The portions of day and night, forenoon, and so forth.
And the seasons are five:

children.text: / hemantito graismiko vārṣiko mitavārṣik. dīrghavārṣika iti /
children.translated_text: Winter, summer, rainy, short-rainy, and long-rainy.
The first two are of four months each.
The next is one month.
Then by day and night.
Less than that, the last is three months.
He should announce [his] dependence (<s>niḥśraya</s>).
The offenses entailing defeat (<s>pātanīya dharmas</s>).
And the acts that make one a [true] renunciant.

children.text: / sa[m*]pannatāṃ samyagtayā ca prepsitasyotgrāhya śīlasāmānyagatatārāgaṇe niyuñjīt* /
children.translated_text: Having ascertained the accomplishment and correctness of what is desired, he should appoint him to the general conduct of moral discipline, like the constellation.
In the reflection on the relationship of requisites.
In the [state of] trained cohabitation.
In the performance of the purpose.
[2a4] He should declare the state of equal attainment — the full comprehension of what has not been declared and what has been taken up.
He should appoint [him] to diligent care.
And the explanation of the means for accomplishment.
The procedure for full ordination //
(a) That which pertains to dependence (<s>niḥśraya</s>).
A dependent should not perform what is to be done without looking to [his] dependence [i.e., preceptor].
Except for urination and defecation.
[His duties include:] discarding the tooth-stick; in a monastery with an inspector, reverential salutation of the <s>cetiya</s> (shrine).

children.text: / ekānnaṃ pañcāśavyāmaparyantād vihārato gamanaṃ [2a5] pātracīvarakarmaṇo glānopasthāne kokṛtyaprativinodane pāpakadṛṣṭigatapratiniḥsarge tīvram autsugyam āpadyetāhovatāhaṃ kuryāṃ kārayeyam veti /
children.translated_text: Going from the monastery up to fifty bow-lengths for food taken once [a day]; in the work of bowl and robe; in attending the sick; in dispelling remorse; in the removal of wrong views — one should develop intense eagerness: 'Oh, would that I might do [this], or cause [it] to be done!'

children.text: / praṇidhātukāme saṃghe ho vata saṃgho syedaṃ praṇidhikarma na kuryād iti /
children.translated_text: When one wishes the <s>Saṃgha</s> to impose [discipline]: 'Oh, would that the <s>Saṃgha</s> perform this act of discipline!'
When [the act] has been performed, he should make [the offender] dwell [in probation].

children.text: / parivāsamūlaparivāsamānāpy amūlamānāpy āvartaṇārthini niḥśraye ho vata saṃghasya parivāsādi catuṣkaṃ dadyād ā[2a6]bṛhet iti /
children.translated_text: For one seeking reinstatement (<s>āvartaṇa</s>) — even one undergoing probation, root-probation, honor-penance, or root-honor-penance — in dependence: 'Oh, would that the <s>Saṃgha</s> give the fourfold [procedure] beginning with probation and complete [the rehabilitation]!'

children.text: / so py etad asmai kuryād utsṛjyāvalokanaṃ /
children.translated_text: He too should perform this for him, having relinquished [his] supervisory observation.
One who has not [completed] nineteen years should not perform full ordination, preceptorship, dependence, or residence of dependents.
Not for one who is not endowed [with qualifications], by association with those next [in seniority], when no one [senior is available].

For the purpose of the boundary (<s>sīmā</s>), in the doing and causing [of duties] — attending the sick, dispelling remorse, removing wrong views, [caring for those in] states of dissatisfaction, and closing [of the eyes of the dead].
Due to the nature of watchfulness, in a group of not less than five, [one should have] learning along with moral conduct.
Knowledge of the [Vinaya] <s>Piṭaka</s>.
Capability in the apprehension of these [matters].
Training [others] in higher morality, higher mind, and higher wisdom.
Or capability in training.
Likewise [regarding] higher conduct, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Prātimokṣa</s>.
Possession of faith, morality, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
In morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge-and-vision [of liberation].
And [the quality of] having undertaken exertion and being wise.
Being mindful.
Being inclined to seclusion.
Being composed.
The state of a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>).
The state of one beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>).
Knowledge of origination, designation, further designation, rejection, and authorization.
Knowledge of what constitutes impediments and non-impediments; the status of declared instructor.
Together with the capability of apprehension, whether of one who is dependent or not dependent.
By means of offenses: knowledge of the gravity and lightness of offenses, and the extent of the current <s>Prātimokṣa</s>.
In the absence of elders, one should take dependence upon a junior [monk].
One should omit only the reverential salutation (<s>sāmīcī</s>).
One who is not a dependent may wander [independently] after five years, in the company of one endowed [with qualifications], on a country-touring circuit.
Not another, even one versed in the three [<s>Piṭakas</s>].
That which pertains to dependence //
(b) That which pertains to those to be admitted.

children.text: / māsi tīrthya iti pravrajyārtham upasaṃkrāntaṃ pṛcched upasampādakāś ca /
children.translated_text: In [each] month, one should ask one who has come from a non-Buddhist sect (<s>tīrthya</s>) seeking going forth; and the ordainers [should ask] too.

children.text: / nānārādhitacittam utsṛjya śākyam āgneyañ ca jaṭilaṃ tīrthyaṃ pravrajayeyur upasaṃpādayeyur vā kṛte tattīrthyānārādhitāditīrthyānta[ra]varjam* /
children.translated_text: Having set aside one whose mind has not been won over, they should ordain and fully ordain a <s>Śākya</s>, a fire-worshipping <s>jaṭila</s> (matted-hair ascetic), and a sectarian — except for one who, after having been ordained, [returns to] an unwon sect or [goes to] another sect.

children.text: / ratnānāṃ varṇasya [2b4] tīrthyānām avarṇasya bhūtasyoktāv akupyatvamārādhitacittatā /
children.translated_text: In the speaking of the truth regarding the [Three] Jewels, and of the [true] color [of the teaching], and of the non-truth regarding the sectarians — [one attains] the state of non-anger and a won-over mind.

children.text: / tadartham atadvan tam enaṃ kṛtopāsakatāntaṃ caturo māsān parivāsayed* saṃgho datvā parivāsaṃ karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: For that purpose, for one who is not of that [qualified] kind, having completed up to the <s>upāsaka</s> [status], the <s>Saṃgha</s> should make him observe probation for four months, giving probation by formal act.
From the <s>Saṃgha</s>, his food.
From the preceptor, [his] robe.
And the agency of the non-giving of the act [belongs to the <s>Saṃgha</s>].
One who has completed fifteen years of age — thus one should ask one who has come seeking going forth.

children.text: / nonam asamarthaṃ kākoḍḍāyane samartham vā [2b5] saptavarṣaṃ pravrajayeyuḥ /
children.translated_text: They should not ordain one under [fifteen who is] incapable; but one capable of scaring crows, even [if only] seven years old, they may ordain.
One [preceptor] should not station more than one novice attendant (<s>śramaṇoddeśa</s>).

children.text: / aruciś ced anekadhyaṃ pravrajyāyāṃ pravrajyātiriktam upasam*pādayet* /
children.translated_text: If there is reluctance [on the part of the preceptor] regarding multiple ordinations, he should fully ordain [them] beyond the going-forth [number].
If [the preceptor] is insufficient, he should hand over [the candidate's] purpose to another for dependence.
That [other] should not seize him [back].
If one does not give [permission], he should fully ordain by forcibly taking [the candidate], when [the preceptor is] angry.

children.text: / vyasiste kasyacit kicid deyam alpaṃ vā prabhūtam vā /
children.translated_text: When someone is in difficulty, something should be given — whether little or much.
One whose father is alive [should not be ordained] without permission.
[2b6] For one seeking going forth from a near region of those two [parents], one should wait seven days.

children.text: / nānārocitaṃ dūradeśam apy enaṃ saṃghe pravrājayet* /
children.translated_text: Even one from a far region who has not been announced — him the <s>Saṃgha</s> should ordain [anyway].
It is proper for the <s>Saṃgha</s> to give food to one seeking going forth.

children.text: / kṛtānujñāte so mātapitṛbhyām ante muktvā dūradeśakaṃ /
children.translated_text: For one who has received permission from both mother and father — at the end, excluding one from a far region.
In [each] month, one should ask one who has come [saying] 'I am sick.'

children.text: / mā te glānyaṃ kañcid astīti vā /
children.translated_text: Or: 'Is there not any illness in you?'
The ordainers [should ask] especially.
They should not ordain or fully ordain a sick person.
When [the act] has been done, [it is valid] from the prior intention.
And [provided] there is no tendency to relapse for him.
Not [valid for] the ordination of one who bears the mark [of another sect] in this way.
One who is created [by magical means].
A <s>paṇḍaka</s> (sexually indeterminate person).
The five kinds of this: by birth, by attachment to a particular fortnight, by manifestation, by jealousy, and made by circumstance.

children.text: / antyasyātra doṣabhaktau nāśanaṃ / steyasaṃvāsikaḥ / jānato kṛtatāṃ vidher upasaṃpado prarūḍhatām vā dvitīyāyāṃ saṃghe na sā[3a2]rdhaṃ karmaṇaḥ pratyanubhūtatāyāṃ tatvaṃ /
children.translated_text: Of the last, the destruction [of <s>paṇḍaka</s> status arises] in the portion of fault. A 'thief of communal life' (<s>steyasaṃvāsika</s>) — [defined as] one who knowingly performs the procedure of full ordination or who has the second [unauthorized ordination] proliferate in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, [or] in the experience of the act together [with the <s>Saṃgha</s>] — that is [the definition].
A 'gone-over to the sectarians' (<s>tīrthikāvakrāntaka</s>).

children.text: / samāttedaṃ pravrajyasya taddṛṣṭer nikṣipyedaṃ cīvaran tena dhvajena tatrāruṇodgamane tattvaṃ /
children.translated_text: One who, having taken up this going forth, having set aside this robe in favor of that [sectarian] banner due to that [sectarian] view — there, at the rising of dawn, that is [the definition].
When [the formal act] has not been done, for the purpose of the matter, just as for the thief [of communal life].
A matricide.
A patricide.
A slayer of an <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One).
A schismatic of the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
One who has drawn blood from the <s>Tathāgata</s> with malicious intent.
A defiler of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun).

children.text: / caturṇāṃ [3a3] pārajikānām anyat tam āpattim āpannaḥ /
children.translated_text: [2b3] One who has committed any other offense among the four <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) offenses.

children.text: / bhyupapataḥ syāc cet sāmagrī punaḥ praṇidhānaṃ /
children.translated_text: If one who has committed a <s>bhyupapata</s> [offense] — if the conditions are complete, [there may be] re-imposition of discipline.

children.text:
/ adarśanoktau mṛṣā cet prāyaścittikaṃ /
hastachinnāḥ pādachinnā aṅgulīphaṇahastakāḥ /
children.translated_text:
If one speaks falsely regarding what was not seen or stated — it is a <s>prāyaścittika</s> (expiatory) offense.
Those with hands cut off, feet cut off, with finger-fan hands,

children.text:
/ anoṣṭakāś ca citrāṅgā ativṛddhā atibālakāḥ /
/ khañjaḥ kāṇḍarikaḥ kāṇaḥ kuṇiḥ kubjo tha vā manaḥ /
/ galagaṇḍamūkabadhirāḥ pīṭhasarpī [3a4] ślīpadī /
/ strīchinnā bhārachinnā mārgachinnāś ca ye narāḥ /
/ tālam uktā kandalichinnāḥ evaṃrūpa hi puruṣāḥ pratikṣiptā maharṣiṇā /
/ prāsādikaś ca pravrajyā pariśuddhasyopasaṃpadā /
/ ākhyā[tā] satyanāmnā vai saṃbuddhena prajānatā /
/ saṃgrāhyagataṃ samāptañ ca pravrajyavastu // #
children.translated_text:
those without lips, those with mottled bodies, the very old, the very young,
the lame, the one with severed tendons, the one-eyed, the crippled, the hunchbacked, or the insane,
those with goiters, the mute, the deaf, those who move on a board, those who crawl, those with elephantiasis,
those cut by women, cut by burdens, cut by the road — such men,
those declared as 'palm[-tall],' those cut by quarrel — such types of persons are rejected by the Great Sage.
And going forth is gracious, full ordination is for the pure;
thus declared by the one of true name, the fully Awakened One, the Knower.
The section on those to be admitted is completed, and the Chapter on Going Forth //
(<s>Vin</s> 1,3) The Section on Miscellaneous [Rules] and Others
A royal servant (<s>rājabhaṭa</s>) [who has been made to do forced labor].
One not permitted by the king, from a near region.
[3a5] One who kills human hostages (<s>narodhvajavadha</s>).
One should not ordain chariot-makers, <s>caṇḍālas</s>, <s>pukkasas</s>, and those of similar [low] kind.
Examples [of the physically disqualified] are those with hands cut off and so forth.

children.text:
/ hāridrakeśā harikeśā haritakeśās tathaiva ca /
/ avadātakeśāś ca ye narā nāgakeśā akeśakā /
/ ghāṭāśirā badraśirā atisthūlāś cipāṭakāḥ /
/ kharasūkaraśīrṣāś ca dviśīrṣā apy aśīrṣakāḥ /
/ hastikarṇā aśvakarṇā gaṇa[3a6]margaṭakarṇakāḥ /
/ kharasūkarakarṇāś ca ekakarṇā akarṇakāḥ /
/ lohitākṣā tivadrākṣāś cullākṣātipiṅgalāḥ /
/ kācākṣā budbudakṣāś ca ekākṣāpy anākṣakāḥ /
/ hastināsāśvanāsā goṇamargaṭanāsakāḥ /
/ kharasūkaranāsāś ca ekanāsā [a]nāsakāḥ /
/ hastijoḍā aśvajoḍā goṇamargaṭajoḍakāḥ /
/ kharasūka[3b1]rajoḍāś ca ekajoḍā ajoḍakāḥ /
/ hastidantāśvadantā goṇamargaṭadantakāḥ /
/ kharasūkaradantāś ca ekadantā adantakāḥ /
/ atigrīvā agrīvāś ca skandhākṣā api kubjakāḥ /
/ lāṃgulachinnā vātāṃḍā ekāṇḍāpy anaṇḍakāḥ /
/ atidīrghātihrasvāś ca kriśāś cātikilāsinaḥ /
/ caturbhiś ca chavivarṇaiḥ khelā vikaṭakās tathā /
/ evaṃvidhā[3b2]nam api taṃ pratikṣepaṃ pradhārayet* /

children.translated_text: One should not ordain a person corrupt in birth or body.
It is proper that one person be ordained by one preceptor with one statement, up to three at most.
There is no mutual performance of the <s>sāmīcī</s> (formal greeting) among those of equal ordination.
Priority is [established] at the time of arrival.

children.text: / na dvyaṅgulād ūrdham āraṇyakaḥ keṣān dhārayet* /
children.translated_text: A forest-dweller should not keep hair longer than two finger-breadths.
This does not [apply] to one near a village, because of the shorter interval.
One should not cut the hair in a curling fashion.
Except around a wound.
One should not have a topknot made.
No hair-treatment in a crowded place.

children.text: / kārayeta vraṇanimittam arūṭṭāv anyathā vijñān* sthavirasthavirān avalokya /
children.translated_text: One may have it done on account of a wound, when unhealed; otherwise, a knowledgeable person should do so after consulting senior elders.
One should not [shave] the body-channel (<s>aṅga-nāḍī</s>) without a proper reason.

children.text: / nānyatra kāye .. kṣurabhāram vā nakhachedaṃ bhajeta vāsimukhaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: One should not apply a razor or nail-cutting or an adze-blade to other parts of the body.
One should not engage in polishing them.

children.text: / bhajeta lekhaṃ malāpakṛṣṭyai na cīvareṇa keśaśmaśrv avatārayet* /
children.translated_text: One should use a scraper for removing dirt; one should not remove hair and beard with a robe.
One should maintain the hair-catching [cloth].
In its absence, [use] the <s>saṃkakṣikā</s> (waist-cloth).
Not on the bedding.
Not where the communal broom falls.

children.text: / avatārayeta prasādādau jīrṇo glāno vātātapavarṣeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: One may remove [hair] during the <s>prasāda</s> period and when old, sick, or during wind, heat, and rain.
One should groom that area.
In a crowded place, a child's tonsure [method should be used].
Likewise for nail-cutting.
A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) who is not supervised should not have her hair cut by a man who is not free from passion.

children.text: / saṃrajyamānām adhiṣṭhātrī samanuśiṣyān* [3b5] smṛtim upasthāpaya kim asmin* pūtikaḍevare sāram astīti /
children.translated_text: The supervisor should instruct one who is becoming attached: 'Establish mindfulness! Is there any essence in this foul carcass?'
The barber should regard [the nun] with the perception of a mother, sister, or daughter.
One should bathe only at the [designated] occasion.

children.text: / pañcāṅgikam vā śaucaṃ na nagnaḥ snāyāt* /
children.translated_text: Or the five-limbed purification; one should not bathe naked.

children.text: / na bhikṣuṇī puruṣatīrthe na strītīrthe cūrṇena /
children.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should not [bathe] at a men's bathing-place, nor at a women's bathing-place with powder.
Powder scented with <s>mudga</s> (green gram) and other fragrances is permitted.
Its acceptance [is allowed].
And that which is infused with medicine [is permitted] for the sick.
A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should not throw powder on a woman.
One should not ascend a staircase that is not tied down, is unstable, has no previous or rear occupant.
One should not be devoted to other deities.
One should not go about with an uncovered face.
One should maintain a bathing-cloth.
Attachment to a double-folded [cloth] exists for living beings [i.e., for modesty].
Even one who possesses the three robes [should do so].

children.text: / patrāṇy abhāve dattvo pūrataḥ pṛṣṭhataś ca pratigupte pradeśe snānaṃ /
children.translated_text: In the absence [of a bathing-cloth], having placed the robes in front and behind in a secluded spot, one should bathe.
By releasing [water], approach to a living being stuck [in it may occur].
In a monastery, this applies to the water-drain.
And the straining of liquid.
The construction of a bathing-hall.
The laying of brick-paving in it.
The release [mechanism] of the water-drain.
The cleaning of the drainage-channel.
After bathing in the drain-pool, no standing up [without draining the water].
One should not clean the body with brick-rubbing or foot-scrubbing, [using one] other [part for another].
This is an illustration for sharp [substances] and lye.
The cleaning of vinegar with fire.

children.text: / na kiñcit kenacid āmuṣṭi celavarter bhikṣuṇy utgharṣet* /
children.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should not rub [herself] with anything by anyone, from the fist-cloth-roller onward.
One should not put on robes while the wash-water with its suspensions has not yet cleared away.
One should maintain a body-wiping [cloth].

children.text: / abhāve muhurtam u<<t*>>kuṭukena sthitvā snātraśāṭakena pocchanaṃ /
children.translated_text: In its absence, having stood crouching for a moment, one should wipe with the bathing-cloth.
One should use the steam-bath.
The construction of a <s>karaṇḍa</s> (basket-furnace) on elevated ground is good.
The release [mechanism] for a ventilation-window — narrow outside, wide inside, ocean-shaped — in the middle.
The installation therein of lattice-windows, shutters, wheels, water-pots, and needles.
And the placing of goat-footed stands.
At the door, the fitting of shutters, bolts, rings, and door-planks.
For the placement of hot water, the making of dove-tail [shelves] on the inner side.
At the fire-place, the laying of brick-paving on the ground.
The banking [of fire] to prevent extinguishing.
For that purpose, maintaining an iron fire-guard.
When the fire is blazing, avoiding entry to prevent exhaustion.
For the prevention of soot-formation, the throwing into the fire of barley-meal smeared with pungent oil.
For the removal of foul smell, the offering of incense.
The arrangement for quick heating with a ball of <s>cikka</s>-paste.
Cleaning with a ball of <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry) paste and <s>pācaka-kṣa</s> (alkaline) compound.

children.text: / tṛṇo bhūmer āstaraṇamātrair autpattikenārdratvena temanena vā /
children.translated_text: The covering of the ground with mere grass-mats, by natural dampness or by steaming.
The making of an iron ladle for the purpose of scratching.
Turning it through a hole and fastening it with a string, in a guarded place with a cover.
For the purpose of ensuring that it does not become dirty, the making of a fire-arrangement therein.
No bathing there [i.e., in the fire area].
The construction of a hall for that purpose.
For the protection of robes from soaking, the making of a brick-enclosed pit.
The release [mechanism] for this water-drain.
When the water is excessively hot, announcing it to the learned.
Breaking [the heat] of it with cold [water].
Sprinkling and other [methods] too.
The provision of a basket filled with stone, cow-dung, tooth-sticks, and other items.
If capable, the preparation of a pre-meal [offering].

children.text: / madhyapātena pratyupatiṣṭhamānam ajñātam atraitgato nirjñānārthaṃ pṛcchet* /
children.translated_text: One entering during the middle period, unrecognized — one should ask this one about their identity for the purpose of ascertaining.
The stationing of a door-keeper for this purpose.
And for the prevention of a <s>bhikṣu's</s> (monk's) entry [at improper times].
One should not grant entry to one without faith.
The performance of service therein together with the monastery's resident pupils.
And with novices — this is another [rule].

Specifically: the provision of lamps, cauldrons, oil, tooth-sticks, cow-dung, clay, powder, water, and other supplies; the inspection of firewood; rubbing, oiling, bathing, sweeping, and the removal of refuse.
These [services] are to be performed mutually among them.
Having cleaned the bench and the vinegar-vessel, placing them in their proper location.

children.text: / sarvatraiṣa bhāṇḍe vidhiḥ sarvam upakaraṃ suguptakelā[y]itaṃ kuryāt* /
children.translated_text: This is the rule for vessels everywhere: one should keep all equipment well-guarded and in good order.
One should enter there with little noise.
[One should be] of pleasing deportment.
One who is well-covered.
Fully aware.
One should not warm oneself standing in front [of the fire].
Avoidance of socializing.
The noble one [should maintain] adherence to silence.
The giving of the three sticks at the end.
One should not perform service wearing only a single robe.
One without faith in the body should not have it performed [on oneself].
Here and in the previous [section], faith must be the governing principle, without haste.
One who is like a lion should not attend upon one who is like a jackal.
But even the most unvirtuous one should attend upon teachers and preceptors.
And also [upon] parents and the sick, even lay people.
Bathing with a compounded bath-preparation.
A bath with decoctions of roots, leaves, flowers, fruits, and such of wind-dispelling and other [medicinal plants] is called that.
After anointing, for the purpose of removing dryness.
With a secondary bath, for the removal of that [oil].
For the earlier purpose, in the final water-pot, giving two or three drops of oil.
One should bathe in a tub.
A sick person should maintain one.
One should place a cover over it.
And a neck-pillow for the cheek [area] therein.
One should not wash the feet just anywhere.
The designated place for this is at the drain-pipe opening.
One should have a foot-washing [basin] made.
Above the monastery, at the northeastern corner.
A turtle-shaped rough [stone basin].
One should set up a clay trough with an elephant-foot-shaped bottom, having a flange.
In the middle, with a <s>kadamba</s>-flower-shaped strainer and a rough [surface].
After washing, the placement [of feet] face-down.
The communal [foot-basin] on the upper terrace.
The personal one in the cell, at the door-joint.

children.text: / pātranirmādanādi yatra pradeśe vihāre kuryāt tasyā mārjanam udakena pralepanam vā /
children.translated_text: The area in the monastery where bowl-cleaning and such is done — its cleaning with water, or plastering.
In the shape of a <s>kunta</s>-fruit or of a <s>mṛdaṅga</s> (drum).
With cow-dung or with clay.

children.text: / na vidyate ratnārthatāyāṃ pralipter ākārasya niyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the purpose is decorative, there is no restriction on the shape of the plastering.
They should not ordain or fully ordain an unfit person.
Not one who is deficient, excessive, or jaundiced.
Three bowls: the largest, the middle, and the smallest.

children.text: / śeṣeṇordhabhāgāntānantarād aṅguṣṭhodarāt pakvatanḍulaprasthasyordhaṃ vā tad dvayāṃ māgadhakasyodvāhi sasūpasavyañjanasyaitan nyāyyaṃ /
children.translated_text: By the remainder — from the end of the upper portion, adjacent to the thumb's belly — half a <s>prastha</s> of cooked rice, or two [<s>prasthas</s>] of <s>Māgadha</s> measure, together with soup and condiment — this is the proper [amount].
A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should not maintain [a bowl] larger than the smallest [size] for a <s>bhikṣu</s>.
At the time of this [ordination] procession, the giving of a tin disc at the sitting-place.
Of a <s>bodhi</s>-<s>vaṭa</s> leaf, or the size of a palm.
And according to measurement.
There is continuity [of the bowl's use] when requested.
Likewise [for] the set of five.
During the rains, one should not be without a bowl.
One should not go on a circuit through the countryside.
One may travel in [times of] danger with a damaged bowl.
One should ordain [another] in [its] absence.

children.text: / notthitaḥ pātraṃ karṣet prakṣipec choṣayed vā /
children.translated_text: One who has stood up should not drag, throw, or dry the bowl.
One should eat in [proper] measure.
One should not throw one's natural waste into it.
One should not sweep refuse with it.
One should not give spittle or hand-mouth-water [into it].
A <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice) whose nature is playful should not clean it.
Not with sandy [substance], not with cow-dung.
One should not store it excessively wet.
One should not neglect it [when] excessively dry.
One should not place it on stone.
Not in an unclean spot.
Not just anywhere.
One should not drop [things] into it.
The making of a rack for this purpose.
For the two who are standing [and] who are circumambulating the monastery — not by digging into the wall.
Of a basket, by forest-dwellers.
Of creepers or of rope.
Plastered with cow-dung and clay.
With a proper fitting lid and cover.
Hanging it on a tree by a hook is good.
Not placing it on the ground.
One should not carry it too far.
One should carry it placed in a bag.
Not by hand.
By the underarm, having given it a carrying-strap for the bag.
One should keep the bowl, medicine, and miscellaneous items in separate bags.
One should maintain them.

children.text: / na tulyāvalambānām āsv ālayanakānāṃ niveśam upayuṃjīta /
children.translated_text: One should not use the same hanging-place for bags of equal suspension [weight].
Nor of those that are not spacious — one wishing to avoid suffering.
To prevent shrinkage, no stuffing in the middle.
For the stability of its positioning, giving [a stitch in] the shape of a crow's foot at intervals.
One should guard the bowl like an eye.
The outer robe like one's skin.
And the remaining robe likewise.
One should not neglect repair.
One should carry out bowl-binding in a guarded spot.
The <s>saṃgha</s> should set up an artisan's workshop.
For a crack, this is unsuitable — [repair it] with molasses, lac, lead-tin, or tin-lead.
Suitable [repairs are made] with strips, pegs, clamps, coral-tooth [pieces].
With powder — of iron or of stone.
Rubbing with oil, because of its resemblance to lead-tin — with iron or with <s>kuruvinda</s> (corundum).
Giving [i.e., applying] when hot.
Having wrapped with birch-bark and smeared with clay — [the firing] of the middle part.

children.text: / ghṛṣṭis tailena guḍamṛdamṛnma[5a5]yasya bhujyamā<<na>>tve pākyatvaṃ māsaṣaṭkānte /
children.translated_text: Rubbing with oil — for a molasses-clay-earthenware [vessel] that is being used, the state of needing firing [occurs] at the end of six months.
If cracked, [firing] after a fortnight.

children.text: / varṣāś cetad virūkṣaṇe mrakṣitatvena kāryāntarāle sya saṃyojyatvaṃ /
children.translated_text: If [it is] the rainy season, for drying this — by being oiled, its joining [is done] in the interval between tasks.
The firing of this.
It is not proper to do this oneself.
The preparation of a pan for that purpose.
Because of its arising from that.
Or of a pot.
Having filled with ashes, proper breaking [is done] with a pot-breaker.
The holding of this.
Covering with that — without counter-smoke.
With an outer coating of husk-and-clay applied.
With oil-cake or cow-dung smeared on the inside, having reached dryness.
On ground that has been prepared, strewn with husks, scattered with charcoal, fine smoke, pot-residue, oil-cake, and such materials — [placing] it upside-down.
Having wrapped with cow-dung or straw, the lighting [of the fire].
The removal [only] when thoroughly cool.
Repetition until the successful production of color is achieved.
Kneading and kneading again, then placing [on the wheel].

children.text: / sāmantakasya prāṇa[5b1]kānām anukampayā sammārjanaṃ sekaś ca /
children.translated_text: Sweeping and sprinkling the surrounding area, out of compassion for living beings.

children.text: / prarohasya parivyañjanam ajñāto varṣāgrasyopasaṃpadyaṅgīkaraṇaṃ vyājenāsya pratyavekṣaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Concealing sprouting [plants]; unknowingly accepting the tip of the rainy season [growth]; by a pretext, the inspection of this.
By means of lowering [from] high clothes-hooks, bamboo-poles, and such.
One should not make [a novice] climb a tree for the purpose of ordination-inspection.
One should not send [him] beyond the boundary.

children.text: / darśanopavicāra enam avakāśane sthāpayeyuḥ gaṇābhimukhaṃ vragṛhītāñjaliṃ* /
children.translated_text: At the assembly for examination of [his] conduct, they should station him in an open area, facing the assembly, with palms joined.
One should not announce the <s>niḥśraya</s> (preceptorship) to a householder.
Nor should one announce it to one who has just been ordained.
They should examine him with the exception of one who presents material work [offerings].
Even a young one — in the absence [of a senior], one should approach the oldest.
Even in the presence [of a senior] — by way of sub-preceptorship.
One should not attend to one of that kind without examination, nor [allow] him [to attend] oneself.
It is faultless — in the absence [of a preceptor] — for one who has begun seeking, who is worthy of preceptorship, or who is unaffiliated — to reside.
Up to the end of five nights.
And worthiness [is established] upon receiving [a preceptor].

children.text: / [5b3] viśramyākantuko dvitīye tritīye vāhni niḥśrayaṃ gṛhṇīt* /
children.translated_text: Having rested, the one without a fixed abode should take preceptorship on the second or third day.
Not for the purpose of a single day.
In the absence of the preceptor, one should approach another.
It is faultless — when not asked, if one who has departed receives work, [and] when that one has not come back.
Not [going] to just anyone's presence.
Having ascertained his conduct, knowledge, retinue, and capacity to benefit — the taking of this [preceptor] through questioning and such, like the <s>saṃvara</s> (ordination vow).
Pressing firmly with both hands upon both soles of the feet.
The giving after examination.
The establishment of the designations of 'son' and 'father.'

children.text: / tatt[ai]vopādhyāy[e] niḥśritatvaṃ tasmād agrahaṇam asya tatra /
children.translated_text: The preceptorship is precisely with that <s>upādhyāya</s>; therefore, the non-acceptance of this from another there.
The attainment of mutual independence — the cause of the destruction of the internal preceptorship of both.
At a gathering, proceeding with one who is not a preceptor but is approved.
With that very one, by that very [authority].
Having seen the preceptor unexpectedly, one should give up one's seat.
Three times a day, one dwelling in the same <s>vihāra</s> should approach the preceptor.
If a forest-dweller, within a <s>krośa</s> (league) — every day.
Every five or six days, if within five <s>krośas</s>.
On the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance) days, if within two or three <s>yojanas</s>.
One should not punish a preceptor-pupil who does not deserve punishment.
There are five [grounds for] punishment.

children.text: / anālāpo navavāda upasthānadharmāmiṣair asaṃbhogaḥ prārabdhakuśalapakṣasamucchedo niḥśrayapratipraśrambhaṇañ ca /
children.translated_text: Non-conversation, the nine [prohibited] speeches, non-enjoyment of offerings of attendance-<s>dharma</s>-food, the cutting off of the commenced wholesome side, and the relaxation of preceptorship.
This worthiness [for punishment belongs] to one without faith.
To one who is lazy, abusive, disrespectful, or who has evil friends.
In the gathering of the punished, if he deposits [his belongings], it is a gross transgression.
When the <s>bhikṣu</s> is disrespectful, the effort of an expert [should be made] for his correction.
For one who has abandoned the cause [of offense], the forgiving by the one who forgives.
One should not punish one who is undeserving.
One should not forgive one who is deserving [of punishment].
One should not forgive one who is undeserving [of forgiveness].
Complete expulsion — when incorrigibility [is established], from persistence.
Having given the filtering-pot and water-strainer, and the upper and under garments — for a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice).
If one looking toward ordination — the five requisites.
And for one who has been ordained.
One should not be a lion-watcher (one who merely watches the preceptor like a show).
They should not perform an act that leads to obstruction.
The purification and freshness of the mouth.
One should use the tooth-stick.
In a concealed [manner].
And the acts of defecation and urination [should also be done in a concealed manner].
Not at the end of a tree or wall that is being used.
Its measure — from twelve finger-breadths up to eight.
Up to four more — in the absence [of the standard], for one who has much phlegm.
There is no impropriety for one who is alone, in hiding [it], upon a rubbish-heap.
There is no failure of concealment here — at the mouth of a drain-pipe.
The hand's vicinity — here, in such a situation, for the purpose of contemplation.
One should scrape one's tongue with it.
One should prepare a tongue-scraper.
Made of needle-material [i.e., metal].
A split tooth-stick is suitable for three purposes.
The mutual rubbing of this — for making it not-sharp.

children.text: / na tīkṣṇena dantaṃ jihvāṃ karṇañ cotghṛṣet* /
children.translated_text: One should not scrape the teeth, tongue, or ears with a sharp [instrument].
Nor with [instruments unsuitable for] eating.
Without harming — for that month.

children.text: / nāprakṣālya digdhaṃ mukhamalena pradeśam a[6a3]vaguṇṭhya vā pāṃśunā dantajihvayoḥ yavanaṃ chorayet* /
children.translated_text: One should not, without washing, [use one] smeared with face-dirt, nor, having covered the area with dust, scrub the teeth and tongue.
Not without making a sound [of warning].
This is illustrative.
Feces, urine, phlegm, nose-blowing, vomit, purging, and other [excretions] as well.
Even from this, the suitability of cleaning — even from alkaline earth, cow-dung, and such.
The robe (<s>cetya</s>) — immediately after the performance of bodily duties, one should pay reverence.
Now, the duties toward the preceptor.
After this — in the morning, having approached [the preceptor], paying reverence.
Asking after [his] health.
Offering alkaline earth, water, and tooth-stick.
Inspecting the kitchen and making announcement.
Making mental note of what is pleasant as something to be offered.
Cleaning the bowl.
If he is an alms-collector — [cleaning] the strainer as well.
With purpose — [cleaning] the filter as well.
If there is a request from him also.

children.text: / sāhyaṃ ced abhirucitaṃ tenaiva saha praveśaḥ /
children.translated_text: If companionship is agreeable — entering together with him.
Going ahead in uneven [terrain] and such.
Turning over to him what has been prepared.
If not accompanying — upon arrival, showing [what was collected].
Offering the superior [portion].
He should know the proper measure everywhere.
Filling the water-vessel.
Announcing the time [for the meal].
After eating — cleaning the bowl and such.
Storing it.
At the [time of] paying reverence to the robe and such — bringing forward the alkaline earth and water.
Performing the duties associated with foot-washing.
Preparing the bed and seat.
Handing over the under-garment.
Receiving the [day-]garment.
Offering the foot-water stand and stool, and the lifting of sandals.
Seeing one who has picked up a broom without permission, as if to perform cleaning duty — one should show slight eagerness [to help].
And [seeing] one who has picked up a needle without permission, as if for robe-sewing duty [— likewise].
Also in the novice's sphere — preparing allowable [foods], obtaining small vegetables, heating, collecting flowers and fruits, gathering tooth-sticks, and such.
One should awaken one who is inside by [tapping with] a peg or such.
This [should be done] gently.
Not too late [in the morning].
One should not annoy him excessively.

children.text: / śanaiḥ saṃ[6b1]prajānan* praviś[e]n niṣkrāmec cāsaṃgharṣayaṃ dvāraśākhe /
children.translated_text: Slowly, with full awareness, one should enter and exit — without scraping the door-jamb.
He should make him [the novice] do this.
One should attend [to him].
Not [doing] what is contrary to that.
One should be modest in this regard.
One should be skillful in his [the preceptor's] duties.
One who performs good deeds, proceeding with grace.
Possessed of modesty and respect.
With deference.
Of humble mind.
Mindful, not neglecting one's own duties.
Seeking to know what is wholesome.
One should prevent [the preceptor] when he is about to commit an offense.

children.text: / avṛddhau kuśale nānyatra tat(kara)kare samarpa[6b2]ṇāṃ yācet* /
children.translated_text: When there is no growth in wholesome [qualities] — unless by that [preceptor's own] hand, one should not request transfer [to another].
Having ascertained — one should assign [him] to the preceptor.
The removal of evil friends.
Employment in wholesome [activities].
Gathering that [wholesome activity]; in a case of transgression, for the purpose of correction — exertion in the attainment of livelihood, requisites, and conformity.

One should attend to a sick person — whether a co-dweller, pupil, <s>upādhyāya</s>, <s>ācārya</s>, one with the same <s>upādhyāya</s>, one with the same <s>ācārya</s>, a conversant, one who has conversed, one who is praised, or one who is beloved.
In the absence of the former [in the list], the next [should attend].
The recitation-teacher too is included here.

children.text: / [6b3] sā hy aśaktau niḥśritaṃ yena pravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: For when [one is] unable, the preceptor [assigns] the one through whom action proceeds.
One who has gone forth — here, one who has assumed that outward mark.
They should not neglect a sick fellow-celibate.
In his absence, they should provide an attendant — not from the end [i.e., the most junior].
Medicine from the <s>Saṅgha</s> is suitable.
For the sole use of the sick person.
If he is not [receptive to] that — the attendant should persuade him.
When there is no supply — they should give from the <s>Saṅgha's</s> [stores].
In the absence [of that] — from the Buddha-property, up to [the value of] a body-journey [i.e., minimal subsistence].
They should make expenditures for conveyance, umbrella, and such, designating him, from the <s>Saṅgha's</s> [property].
In the absence of that — from the Buddha-property.

children.text: / deyatvam ā[bhy]ām āttasya tenāmṛtyau sati vibhave /
children.translated_text: What has been taken by both — the obligation to return it upon recovery, when there is ability.
The attendant should not fail to attend to him.
Nor should he contravene the <s>dharma</s>-teachings and instructions regarding his [the patient's] needs.
When asked [for items] that are the means of final [preparation], one should not withhold.
One should not fail to address him.
A sick person should not step over him [the attendant].

children.text: / sāṃghikād enam asau māraṇāśaṃkāyāṃ śayanāsanād utthāpya [6b5] pautgalike niveśayeta /
children.translated_text: When there is apprehension of death, that one [attendant] should lift him from the <s>Saṅgha's</s> bed and seat and place him on a personal [bed].
Under the pretext of anointing and bathing first.
One should be diligent in discerning the stages of that [dying] condition.
The washing of robes soiled by that [dying process] and of the deceased's robes — that is the proper task of that [attendant].
The <s>Saṅgha</s> should go first to the assembly of elders at that place.
One who is delayed in going — one should wait for [him].
And they [should wait] for him.
And one who has not departed — having gone a long distance.
And at the village boundary.
If entering here — [others] should follow along.

children.text: / drutaś cet* syād āgamaya yāvat sthavirāgaccha[6b6]tītenaṃ brūyuḥ /
children.translated_text: If he is fast — they should say to him, 'Wait until the elder comes.'

children.text: / pāṇyudakadāne ca gatatve bhyavahārāyāsti cet* kālaḥ -
children.translated_text: And in the matter of offering hand-water — when he has gone, if there is time for a meal —
When there is no formal seating here — they should give up the seat.
When [the elder] is seated — one should also attend [to matters] outside.

children.text: / duḥprāvritatve durnivastatāyāṃ vā sauṣṭhavārtham anayor nimittam asmai kurvīt* /
children.translated_text: When poorly clothed or badly dressed — for the sake of propriety, one should make a cause for these two [defects to be remedied for] him.
If there is no objection — one should have [it] done through an intermediary.
When there is no supply — one should not oneself engage the juniors in conversation.

children.text: / yatreṣām vihārāraṇyayor vṛttis tat vṛttaṃ grāhayen niyuñjī /
children.translated_text: Where their livelihood is, in <s>vihāra</s> or forest — that conduct one should teach [them] and assign.
Having examined a visitor — one should announce [him] to the residents for the purpose of [providing] bed and seat.

children.text: / gamiko diksārthāvāsaśayanāsanaṃ sahāyakāBś ca glānyena pahāyitvena tolayitvā prakrāmet* /
children.translated_text: One who is departing should set out, having weighed the purpose of the direction, the quarters' lodgings and beds, and companions — with illness and [the risk of] loss.

children.text: / sarva paścāt mā kasyacit kiñcit pramuṣitam ity apetya dūram utsārayet* /
children.translated_text: Afterward, saying 'Let nothing be stolen from anyone,' having gone some distance, one should move all [belongings] away.
One should settle the juniors with humility and without arrogance.
All should [attend to] all who have entered the family [of the Saṅgha].

And knowing — one should benefit [them] by accomplishing what needs to be done: instruction and teaching of the noble ones, food-offerings, obtaining [requisites], arrangements for the sick, and such.
One who has entered the rains-retreat should make [others] repair a <s>vihāra</s> that is not being repaired, having informed [them].
One should encourage [one who is] repairing.
Everyone should benefit those who have come to an assembly, when a discourse is desired, with a conclusion in accord with the <s>Dharma</s>.
One should disregard those delighting in silence.
One should share food with a householder who has approached.

children.text: / akaraṇe niṣṭau vā dharmyām ebhyaḥ kathaṃ kṛtvedam asmākaṃ saṃvidyata iti brūyāt* /
children.translated_text: If [they are] not doing so, or at the conclusion, having given them a <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, one should say: 'This is our arrangement.'
Everyone who has that [qualification] should examine the assembly.
One should restrain one who conducts himself wrongly.
Coming and going and such therein should be done as [prescribed] here.
One should not engage in miscellaneous cross-talk.

One should not stand [in his way].
When addressed, one should speak or carry out [the instruction].
One should not interrupt a conversation in the middle.
One should oppose one who speaks <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
One should approve of <s>Dharma</s>.
One should accept a rightfully arisen gain.
One should be unexcited in a household, standing without arrogance.
With upcast eyes.

One should engage them in giving, self-restraint, discipline, celibacy, dwelling [in virtue], <s>poṣadha</s> (observance), taking refuge, and undertaking the training-rules.
In all situations that are a gateway to transgression, one should proceed mindfully.
One who has fallen should not be a follower.
To one who has arrived, one should respond with 'Come! Welcome!' and prior pleasant conversation.
With an open, bright countenance, remembering previous [meetings], with brow unfurrowed.

children.text: / gṛhī cet* dharmyām asmai kathaṃ kuryāt* /

children.text: / [7a5] anāgacchaty atra grāmāntikas saṃrañjanīyaṃ yathāśakti pravartayet* /

One should set up water and a seat.
Sweeping, [preparing] beds and seats, announcing, placing water, serving — a novice should perform these along with food-distribution.

children.text: / upagacched vilomāṃ parijanakriyāṃ na cet svaparopaghātāya /
children.translated_text: One should attend to the servant's menial work, provided it does not cause harm to oneself or others.

children.text: / asmai cec chaktau samucchidyaināṃ dharmyām utpādya tayā saṃjñapayeta /
children.translated_text: If able, one should uproot that [wrong practice], produce a righteous one, and with that correct [the servants].

children.translated_text: One who does not submit — having announced it, having him seized suddenly by some prince's friend, minister, officer, prince's man, or servant — should be expelled in a purification assembly.
A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> [stands] in the place of a <s>bhikṣu</s> for all ordinations.

Only for one who has taken dependence [on a teacher].

The growth [of faults] from the time of her ordination being less than that [is treated] beginning with that.
Twelve years of age is the beginning for one who has been married at full ordination.
The establishment [of the status] is through the conferral.

By the <s>saṃgha</s>.

In the absence of full ordination, [it applies] to his.

Not among the naked, the angry, those of masculine appearance [who are female], or women with male characteristics.

A minor offense only, at the first occurrence.
Without the consent of the preceptor.
When an impediment is not asked about, when it is declared though not existing, and when given [ordination despite it].

children.text: / na puruṣānukṛtitvaṃ striyā stryanukṛtitvaṃ ca puruṣasya vyañjanāntaraprakāraḥ /

One with a single nail, one with ocean-lines, one wing-struck, one with the mark of a head[-shape], one with a hidden goiter, one with hair inside and outside, one doubly hunchbacked, one with six companions, one without fingers, one with consumption, one like a mongoose, one like a <s>kiṃpila</s> (a kind of fish), one reversed, one with joined [features], one with suspended, one with blinking, one blind, one with disease of the eyes, one with <s>śāla</s>-tree affliction, one with <s>dadru</s> (ringworm), one with <s>vicarcikā</s> (eczema), one yellow, one white, one red, one with [visible] veins in the ears, one with <s>kaṇḍū</s> (itching), one lumpy, one stout, one with <s>kacchu</s> (scabies), one with trembling limbs, one with concealed [defects], one confused, one without a tongue, one with a single hand or foot, one with blue hair, one like an elephant, horse, dog, cow, goat, deer, fish, or snake, one with a long or many heads, one with a <s>tāla</s>-throat, one with spear[-shaped] affliction, one with gait impairment — and from those [with conditions that are] not impediments, by a sick person; for the rest [who have permanent conditions, ordination is barred].

Not for those of non-human destiny.
There is no arising [of ordination] from the <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) offenses.
This should be reversed by the parents.
Not by both [parents acting together, but each separately]
The nature of this act is authoritative for cases beginning with matricide.
Corruption through non-celibacy by both parties when not defeated.

Section 2: The <s>Poṣadha</s> (observance) section.
The <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) offenses.

[The method of renunciation]

Not with the perception of privacy.

children.translated_text: The training [is renounced by saying]: 'I renounce the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>Vinaya</s>, the <s>Mātṛkā</s>, the teacher, the preceptor, the household-maintaining-ascetic-designation, the eunuch, the corrupter of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, the one living in theft, the one of different communion, the one without communion, the non-Buddhist ascetic, one entered into non-Buddhist practice, the matricide, the patricide, the slayer of an <s>Arhat</s>, the splitter of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, one who with malicious intent has drawn blood from a <s>Tathāgata</s> — "Enough for me of celibacy with those like you, or of communal living, or of dwelling and enjoyment!"' — these are the renunciation-statements.
The method of renunciation.
(a) That pertaining to the <s>vibhaṅga</s>.
The acceptance of intentional entry and emission.
In that [context]:
When unimpaired [in the sexual organ].
In the mouth or in the rectum.
When [those organs are] impaired, it is a grave offense (<s>sthūla</s>).
When there is lack of capacity, a reduction [in penalty].
No reduction in [cases of] non-human destiny, being a eunuch, a hermaphrodite, one who always practices, one who has an intermediary, or one who is dead.
When there is non-intention, destroyed nature, or non-arousal — when there is no entry.
For one who is being practiced upon, in the case of his own [organ being used].
When preceded by external friction, not when released internally — in the case of it belonging to another.

Three forms of guarding.
The state of being in an enclosed, surrounded place with a closed door; being watched; having the lower garment knotted by the monks.
The analysis of the <s>pārājika</s> of non-celibacy.
(b) That pertaining to the <s>Kṣudraka</s>.
One should not approach the place where one would be desired by a woman.
One should not dwell where a non-human being is prepared for touch.
One of intense passion should maintain a sheath.
Of goat-skin, deer-skin, or rat-skin.
For the purpose of preventing foul smell from alkaline [substances].
Cleaning and drying [of it].
Another [sheath] for temporary purposes.
When liquid has been produced in abundance, giving of a [protective] spread.
Of sand or of dust.
Having set it aside, having performed purification, [then] meal[-taking] and <s>caitya</s>-veneration.
That pertaining to the <s>Kṣudraka</s> on the <s>pārājika</s> of non-celibacy.
(c) That pertaining to questions.
The beginning of the mouth is beyond the teeth.
Of the rectum, from the end of the <s>vilagaṇḍikā</s> (the anal sphincter).
Of the urinary passage, from the skin-fold.
The entry of the glans — that is [considered] inside.

children.translated_text: Of a region: being bitten is the eighth — being bitten, being empty, being moistened, being struck, being eaten by creatures — this is impairment.

children.translated_text: And when there is no awareness of the joint, of one who is split, of the middle-region that is being used, of one who is joined together.
When there is awareness, the next stage [of offense].
A grave offense for a cooked [corpse], one without hair, a pig and such.
When the head is severed, [offense pertains to] the mouth.
When separated, of the bodily [acts]: excessive use and [normal] use.
Of two others' [organs] also, belonging to another — when joined elsewhere.
Of another, when the body is severed — of a [remaining] orifice.
Of the adjacent approachable [organ] — in the case of a tumor.
Of the two lips.
Of the external [organ], beyond the boundary.
Of the urethra.
Doubled in [the cases of both] touch and entry.

children.translated_text: The interposition mentioned last — intended by which, the entire [offense] of one who is interposed is not [entirely] impossible with regard to touch.

/ anyenāntaritatvam aspṛṣṭipraveśena vyākhyātaṃ //
prathame pārājike pṛcchāgataṃ //

Being interposed by another is explained as non-touch and non-entry.
The question-based material on the first <s>pārājika</s> [is complete].
