For one who has the intention of taking what is white [i.e., pure/innocent] without apprehension — the arising of fault.
When a commodity is of that nature — it should be given [back].
When [something is] released, crossing over another's [boundary] is not theft.
What is not released — one should not have another cross over [with it].
If the crossing is unintentional and does not succeed — one does not fall [into the offense].
The stationing of a guard — of more than one <s>bhikṣu</s>.
The collectibility of his food-portion.
Prevention by that [guard].
Announcement when [something is] thrown [into the community store].
Making a mark when [identification is] not possible.
Concealment in the case of taking [by a thief].
The tangibility of what has not been obtained — of that which is to be removed otherwise.
The delivered nature of what has not been caused to fall — when there is certainty of the approached [person's acceptance].
Praise to the parents for the purpose of [their] inclination toward that [gift].
And of precious things.
Giving for the purpose of another, from another's [property] — a loan-taking debtor.
One should not divide [goods] that require duty-payment with the carrying-load.
Non-applicability [of the offense] to a dyed [robe] — even when squeezed out with cow-dung.
And when its edge is cut — of this [too].
Non-ascent [of the offense] when the intention regarding that [is present] but not seen [in action].
One should not strike at another's turn [i.e., another's rightful share].
One should not cultivate trust in one who is untrustworthy.
Applicability [of the lower offense] for a lower [garment] in the case of the upper [garment].

children.text: / pṛyo sau manāpo gurur bhāvanīyaḥ pūjyaḥ praśasyaḥ pretāgrahaṇena /
children.translated_text: 'He is dear, pleasing, a guru, worthy of honor, worthy of praise' — by taking [another's property] through the pretext of [devotion to] the departed.
One should perform work as a reciprocal act, and with the thought of merit.
Not for wages.
[9b3] No calamity [arises] from [errors in] regional vocabulary.
One should not keep [property that has] fallen [to one] through a corrupt mind for too long.
What belongs to the keeper of possessions (<s>upadhivārika</s>) should be given [back].
In the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s estimation of one who has been ordained by him — showing [the evidence].
When the owner does not approve — binding in the case of [unauthorized] repair.

children.text:
/ nānanujñātāt glānena tatbhaṣajyaṃ pācet* //
adattādānapārājayike vibhaṅgaḥ //
children.translated_text:
A sick [monk] should not prepare that medicine from one who has not given permission. //
The analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>) in the <s>pārājika</s> of taking what is not given //
(b) That which pertains to miscellaneous [rules].

children.text: // na saparigrham anujñā[t]o nyena kalpena svīkuryāt* /
children.translated_text: One who has [property in his] possession should not appropriate [it] in another manner without permission.
One should not release what has been accepted.
[9b4] Ask him by means of a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching.
And for half the price.
It is proper to take even a cracked bowl or robe.

children.text: / nāsatsaṃbhāvanā vā hy utsṛṣṭam ity amahājanapratyakṣam adhitiṣṭhet* /
children.translated_text: One should not stand upon wrong estimation — that which has been discarded — [unless it is] in the sight of the public.
When there is no non-human custody, a corpse's property has the nature of non-ownership.
Going behind one who is corrupt.
Giving from the feet upward to one who has fallen face-down.
One should not take from one who does not [verbally] give permission.
One should not excavate himself, nor cause [another] to excavate.

children.text: / pratiśamanam eva dantakā[9b5]ṣṭho .. koṣāḍukagomayamṛdāṃ yathāsukhakaraṇaṃ dhāraṇam akāmaṃ saṃbaddhenāpahṛyamānasya bhikṣoḥ śrāmaṇerasya vā /
children.translated_text: The tooth-stick is only for cleansing; the comfortable holding of a sheath-container of cow-dung and clay [is allowed]; [also,] the involuntary [carrying away] of a <s>bhikṣu</s> or <s>śrāmaṇera</s> being carried off by a bond.
The miscellaneous section in the <s>pārājika</s> of taking what is not given //
(c) That which pertains to questions.
Four <s>kākaṇīs</s> make one <s>māṣaka</s>.
An example: the quality of the fifth from a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>.
Where it has the value of twenty — depending on that.
The determination of this [offense is made] by counting the time, place, and quantity of the carrying.
The state of being at the extreme limit — through the greatness of the price that is impossible to produce.
Not through the smallness — its being lesser is its being included within [a higher category].
The state of being an invaluable jewel — this [applies to] a <s>Buddha</s>-relic.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> [arises] in [its] worship and veneration.
Freedom from fault in the case of a document [i.e., a written deed].
When destroyed and taken — [the object] in that condition has the nature of a thing stolen.
The character of non-ownership [applies] in <s>Uttarakuru</s>.
This is like one's own [property] there.
The ownership of oneself [extends] to what is temporary.
The divine nature of one who has attained <s>nirvṛti</s> (liberation).
The enjoyment of what has been permitted by the one who authorized it — as if it were fully relinquished.
And the giving [of property] through <s>mantras</s> and medicines.
And in the case of acting for another's benefit — the original procedure [applies].
And by proper means.
And the deliberation regarding the desire to steal what is pleasing, in its shadow [i.e., possibility].
The attempt [constitutes] ruin through gambling — if the state of being won is real.
This here is [the definition of] theft.
In the counting of that.
The applicability [of the offense] in the elision and superimposition of a mark.
And when [an object is] deposited above its [original] place.
Completion here [constitutes] theft.
Likewise, the counting [is applied] in another category.

children.text: / vyapalāpaś ca paurvasyetareṣu dvai(n)tarasya vā pūrveṣu /
children.translated_text: And denial — of the former [owner's claim] in the case of the others, or of the second in the case of the former.
Where this [applies] to all beginning [portions] — there [it has] the character of a share.
And the manifesting of one who attains, and [the case] of one who does not originate.
And cooking without having been instructed.
The attempt [constitutes] denial — 'It was begged with the body' — thus, of those who cast [blame] even upon the least.
Bringing [something] to completion [constitutes] theft.

children.text: / nihitanikṣepasya saha ced vyācanena pañcāc cātaḥ purastāc cet prayogāntaratvaṃ /
children.translated_text: Of a deposit held in trust — if together with deception, [the offense is complete] from the fifth [<s>māṣaka</s>] onward; if beforehand — the character of an intermediate attempt [applies].
Destruction [constitutes] a <s>sthūlātyaya</s> (grave transgression); cutting and killing likewise.
The character of <s>sthūlātyaya</s> [applies to] a boundary-space in the breaking of a tax.
Freedom from fault in conveying by supernatural power, and of what is beyond the boundary.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> [arises] from the exertion [of conveying].
And one who points out an alternative path [to the thief].
Less [than the full amount constitutes] a secondary offense.
A path that is not a path [constitutes a violation] like a road.

[10a3] Of another's deposit — when one who has taken it by the mouth and throat [i.e., by swallowing], the last one, [does so] with the intention of stealing — the performance [of the offense is established].
No diminishment [of the offense] through a written [instrument] and the like.
Breaking is not in itself theft.
Nor [the theft] of what remains in its place.
Being killed does not [constitute] the completion [of the offense].
Not by a partial [removal] when [the object is] not released from its place.
Cutting off — when by that removal — [constitutes] theft.
Exit by oozing, trickling, or piercing through a hole.
And the unity of the substance [is maintained] from other than the last [portion].
Taking from a heap [constitutes] a division of theft.
When the agents are not unified — each bite [is a separate offense].
And of the takers.
When they act by unanimous agreement — here [it is] theft [for all] //
// The section on questions in the <s>pārājika</s> of taking what is not given //
(d) Adjudicated cases.
When [the owner] dies before [the thief's] completion — [the object has] the character of being re-depositable.
The character of a dead person's property — in the reverse [case].

children.text: / bhrātṛvat saṃgho na tadarthaṃ hāro na svīkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Saṃgha</s> is like a brother — not theft for that purpose, nor acceptance [by the individual].
Like one's own — no distinction of ownership [within the <s>Saṃgha</s>].
Not [an offense] when taken by the learned without departure [from rules] or when there is determination of taking.
Not [an offense] when one's intention is to accept a share and not [to effect] taking.
Not [an offense for] the performance of the act pertaining to that — nor for him [the custodian].

children.text: / na sārdhamvihāritvaṃ antevāsitā ca hārā[10a5]nutthāne kāraṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Not [an offense] through co-residence or pupilship — the cause [must be] in the non-arising of theft.
In enclosure for the purpose of a boundary — the system [applies].
Not [an offense for] what remains as the boundary-crossing — this does not constitute a charge by him.

children.text: / samakṣānte py anābhāsitvaṃ hāraḥ vaśīkṛtatvaṃ phalāt grahe manuṣyasya /
children.translated_text: Even when in full view — non-summoning [constitutes] theft; subjugation [occurs] through taking the fruit of a human being.
Not this of oneself.

children.text: / na hāre yad abhisaṃhitaṃ tatsaṃbandhād anābhisaṃhita(ṃ)syāpakramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not in theft — what is intended in connection with that; the departure of what is unintended [is not an offense].

children.text: / sthūlaṃ yo yat gṛhṇīte tasya tad iti vyavasthāyām anyahāre /
children.translated_text: A <s>sthūlātyaya</s> — 'whoever takes whatever, that is his' — in the determination of another's theft.
Taking from a cemetery that has [an owner in] possession.
In enchanting by <s>mantras</s> [the products of] a slaughterhouse, dyer's workshop, leaves, flowers, fruit-gardens, and the like.

children.text: / grāsānupradānena nayatāśvam adhirūḍhena caivam eṣa hartavyam iti kāyaviprakāre /
children.translated_text: Leading a horse by giving morsels of feed, and mounted upon it — 'this is how this one should be carried off' — in the bodily gesture.
And a boat.
And [by saying] 'from here.'
When one resolves [to use property] of mother, father, brother, sister, preceptor, teacher, <s>stūpa</s>, <s>Saṃgha</s>, and the like — crossing over the duty-payment and what ought to be done.
When requested [but] in the resolve of not giving to the keeper.
And in the distribution — of what has been given for the purpose of the last [resort].
When one with the perception of [something being] owned [takes from what is] owned.
In the [case of] gruel, boiled rice, fine flour, fish, meat, hard food, raw goods, and alms-round — when [things are] not known through possession — elsewhere [the offense applies] to the substance.
Not [an offense] with what is designated [for one].
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> [arises] for eating when uninvited.
And in going, for the purpose of carrying away.
There should be no deliberation — from that [follows] separateness.
'Without grasping' — thus, having made one's own examination, one should take.
One should not make a bodily concealment.
One should not break into a nest [or receptacle].
One who has not been authorized in that [place] should not claim a share of the rains-season robe.
No fault [arises] in receiving from a thief when [received] with the mind of a donor.
One should not take [goods] from a highway robber who has not come [legitimately], or from a thief-bandit.
[10b2] What has been cut by a weapon — having discolored it, one should keep what has been taken from there.
Even of what has been [previously] so treated — giving [is proper] when asked.
One should not engage in circular exchange.
No fault [arises] in releasing [an animal] by means of <s>mantras</s>.

children.text: / mūṣikāpahṛtasya ca svasyādāne nyabhikṣvarthasya tad arthaṃ /
children.translated_text: And in the taking of one's own [property] carried off by a rat — for the sake of that, when another <s>bhikṣu</s> [acts on behalf of another].
In the taking [of property] of a deer that, pursued by a hunter, has entered an <s>āśrama</s>.

When this one is dead, the obligation to give to them.
The adjudicated cases in the <s>pārājika</s> on taking what is not given.
The <s>pārājika</s> on taking what is not given is complete.
The <s>pārājika</s> on killing.
What is contained in the <s>vibhaṅga</s> (classification).
One should not, in conformity with the intention of death, withdraw provisions from a sick person during care.
One should not, without his knowledge and without his request, prepare the means of opposition to death.
Nor when [death's] course has truly [begun].
Nor [provide] the implements of death.
The attendant should prevent him from that practice [intended] for the purpose of death.
One should not wish for another's death for the sake of [gaining] his property.
The impermissibility of mind — of approving the commission of what should not be done.
Obstruction of a living being [is the offense].
That — with [killing] intention, when directed at a human being.
No distinction [is made] among those [who kill] by body, by what is connected to it, by what is released, or by instigating another.

Of [the means of] killing: poison, powder, a pit, [falling] timber, a destroyed creature, sending [an assassin], a cliff, a letter [of deception], a fraudulent [scheme], a rod, beating, and the application of <s>mantras</s>.
Of throwing into water or fire.
Of exposure to cold or heat.
Of sending on an errand and such — [even] of a minor [nature] in execution.
In the case of the victim being a woman, man, or eunuch.
At another time — when death [results] from that cause.
The absence of grounds [for offense] — from choosing [to kill] another person [than intended].
A gross [transgression] — for one with murderous intent — in the crushing of the womb of a mother and embryo.
But in the assent [to participate] — that being the cause, of the one who has proceeded to kill.
And of one who says, 'I give you the implements of death by name.'
Or in killing another — even one who is magically created — of an animal.
One should not give medicine to a sick person that has not been examined and without being instructed [about it].
Here, the requirement of examination [applies to medicines] for those who are knowledgeable, those who have gone forth, and those who are afflicted.
And by disease.
Of very old <s>bhikṣus</s> who have co-renunciants.
In the absence of the former — [the responsibility falls to] the other.
The absence of a reduction [in offense] when not administering medicine with the desire to benefit, [the result being] death.
One who [is part of a group carrying] an unbearable load should not, in casting [it down], act in a manner that causes harm.

children.text: / bhajeta dūpaś cet pratyayo vyavakīrṇatāyāṃ gṛhasthair niyuktatāyāṃ samotkṣepe /
children.translated_text: One should act with precaution, if there is cause, in the state of being intermingled — when employed by householders, in the simultaneous lifting.
Even in placing — when there is equality, one should employ [others].
One should not throw bricks.

children.text: / na caṭitāṃ sphuṭitāṃ vā nārocya tatvam a[11a1]rpyayeta /
children.translated_text: Nor should one [throw] a cracked or split [brick] without announcing the truth and without [first] handing it over.
One should make a [warning] sound for [distinguishing from] thieves and enemies.
One should throw [things] that have been trimmed — [such as] lumber-heaps and such.
And downwind — dust, pot-fragments, ashes, potsherds.
One should hold [back from throwing when there is] what might be destroyed.
One should not throw [anything at] an exhausted <s>bhikṣu</s>.
The making of provisions for his protection.
Rest [should be provided].
The giving of a bundle [to carry for him].

children.text: / aśaktau prāpṇum āvāsaṃ samaṃ cen na kāle bhaktasya pānakasya vā /
children.translated_text: When [he is] unable to reach the lodging at the same time — if not at the time for food or drink.
The cleaning of the bowl.
The placing of the carrying-frame.
The receiving [of it].
The inspection.

children.text:
/ kāle cet pratyutgamanam ādāya //
vadhapārājayike vibhaṅgaḥ //
children.translated_text:
If at the [proper] time — going to meet [him], taking [his belongings].
The classification in the <s>pārājika</s> on killing.
What is contained in the <s>kṣudraka</s> (minor rules).
The cutting off of a hand of one in human state — a gross [transgression].
In the giving of fire for a conflagration.
In the selling of hair.

children.text:
/ rājakule yena muṣitas tasyārpaṇe /
vadhapārājayike kṣudrakagataṃ //
children.translated_text:
In the case of one robbed at the royal court — handing over to the very one [who robbed him].
The <s>kṣudraka</s>-section in the <s>pārājika</s> on killing.
What is contained in the <s>pṛcchā</s> (questions).
The instruction by appointment.
An illustration — the mother's womb.
A gross [transgression] — in killing oneself.
A difficult [case] — the virtuous act of one whose mind is undisturbed.
There is no agency when the intended result is not accomplished.

There is no ripening of <s>karma</s> in another birth.
The question-section in the <s>pārājika</s> on killing.
The adjudicated cases.

children.text: // sthūlaṃ mṛtyur evaṃ me bhavatīti bruvāṇasyāprati(ya)<<pa>>tā tathātvasaṃpādane mṛyatām ity anusthānaiḥ glānasya /
children.translated_text: A gross [transgression] — when one says 'Thus death comes to me' and, not being contradicted, accomplishes the truth of that through practices — of a sick person.
In giving food that is unsuitable [for the sick person's condition].
In the lancing of an unripe boil.
In causing to fall — into a pit, through a door, a step, and such.
In the practice [intended] for the purpose of death — by a precipice, abandonment, hanging, and such.

children.text: / na glānāya sahasā [11a4] śastrakaṃ rajum vā dadyāt* /
children.translated_text: One should not suddenly give a knife or rope to a sick person.
One should perform one's duties with full awareness.
And one should give the <s>mantra</s>-slap [as a curative measure].

children.text: / prahārañ cāderapanodāya tatbhūtaḥ supratyavekṣitaṃ kṛtva le..yet* /
children.translated_text: And for driving away fear and such — having become such [a healer], having carefully examined, one should [...apply treatment].
One of small portion [i.e., weak] should not undertake a heavy load.
One should not go head-downward.
One untrained should not apply training [techniques].
One should not order a weapon when [only] a verbal [intervention] was called for.

One should not lead a sick person to an incompetent [physician].
The adjudicated cases in the <s>pārājika</s> on killing.
The <s>pārājika</s> on killing is complete.
The <s>pārājika</s> on false claims of superhuman attainment.
What is contained in the <s>vibhaṅga</s>.
Having established perception — the false declaration of oneself as possessing superhuman <s>dharma</s> attainments.

children.text: / tatvaṃ paśyāmi mā paśyanti śabdan* śṛṇomi mama śreṇvanty upakramāmi mānupasaṃkrāmanti sārdham ālapāmi saṃlapāmi pratisaṃmode sātatyam api samāpadye mayā sārdham ity ukte /
children.translated_text: 'I see the truth; they see me; I hear sounds; they listen to me; I approach them; they approach me; I converse with them; I commune with them; I exchange greetings; I enter absorption continuously; and they [do so] with me' — when thus stated.
When imputed to <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>kaṭapūtanas</s>.
A gross [transgression] — regarding a dust-<s>piśāca</s> [a minor spirit].

The contemplations of impermanence and such, the <s>dhyānas</s>, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the fruits [of the path], the <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges), and such — these are the 'higher <s>dharmas</s>.'
A gross [transgression] — regarding one who grasps the specific characteristic [only], who suppresses the <s>kleśas</s> [temporarily], who [attains only] the sign of <s>śamatha</s> (calm).

children.text: / nānuktis tadva tv asya tadvad dharmakatvogtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Non-declaration of that [attainment] — but his [claiming to be] of the nature of one who has that <s>dharma</s>, like one who has it — is speaking [falsely].

children.text: / parāvadeśatvam asty asāv ity upasandhāne svasya /
children.translated_text: Being instructed by another — there is [an offense] when there is self-deception with 'He has that.'
When there is no self-deception [— no offense].

One should not explain without having reflected [carefully].
The classification in the [<s>pārājika</s> on] false claims.
What is contained in the questions.
The declaration of the higher [attainment] — the communicating of attainment or loss — is not [simply an] announcement.
A gross [transgression] — in the declaration of name and meaning with the intention of announcing higher [attainment].
Of the opposite [i.e., the loss of attainment — it is the same].

children.text:
/ saṃsūcanena ca na bhūtottaratve sya jātatvaṃ //
pralāpe pṛcchāgataṃ //
children.translated_text:
And by insinuation — there is no arising [of full offense] when the higher [attainment] is real.
The question-section in the [<s>pārājika</s> on] false claims.
The adjudicated cases.

children.text: / sthūlam arhantadantogracārhasi cīvarādikaṃ brāhma[ṇ]o vāhita<<pa>>āpadharmā ṣaḍgatasyendriyāṇi sudāntaguptarakṣitabhāvitānīty uktasya tūṣṇīmbhāvenādhivāsane /
children.translated_text: A gross [transgression] — when one says to an <s>arhat</s>: 'You are an <s>arhat</s> with teeth and tusks; you deserve robes and such; you are a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has dispelled evil <s>dharmas</s>; one who has [mastered] the six sense-faculties — well-tamed, guarded, protected, and cultivated' — and [the <s>arhat</s>] assents by remaining silent.

children.text:
/ yadi bhadanto rhan piṇḍa[11b2]pā[t]aṃ me gṛhāṇa praviśa gṛhām āsane niṣīda <<ha>>stodakaṃ gṛhāṇa bhojanaṃ pratigṛhāṇa sūpikaṃ bhuṃ[k]ṣvānumodasva niṣkrāmeti tadvat saṃpādane //
pralāpe vinītakāni //
samāpta uttarapralāpaḥ //
children.translated_text:
'If, venerable one, you are an <s>arhat</s> — accept my alms-food, enter the house, sit on the seat, accept hand-water, accept food, eat the broth, give a rejoicing [benediction], and depart' — in accomplishing [the donation] in such a manner.
The adjudicated cases in the [<s>pārājika</s> on] false claims.
The [section on] false claims of superhuman attainment is complete.
The <s>Saṅghāvaśeṣa</s> (offenses requiring formal meeting of the <s>Saṅgha</s>).
The emission of semen.
What is contained in the <s>vibhaṅga</s>.
A dream is as though non-existent [in terms of offense].
The non-culpability of its result.
In [intentional] emission.
With that [specific] intention.
Of one's own semen.
In the first [instance].
No distinction [is made] among [emissions motivated by] pleasure, knowledge, [desire for] seed, medicine, or philosophical inquiry.
By touching.
By exertion.
Of the sexual organ.
Even by an external [object] — a sentient being, positioned, engaged in that activity.
Even without squeezing or pressing.
And by [the experiences of] enjoyment, diffusion, release, and the experience of pleasure.
The non-culpability of [emission] that has not entered the channel — when one is restrained at the stage of being pierced, [having been] celibate since completion.
A lesser [offense] — in dancing and causing to dance.
In hip-movement in the air.
In touching with another part [of the body].
In holding [the organ] against the current.
And against the wind.
Up to the experience of the pleasure of enjoyment.
Of [semen] that has entered the channel.
Not, when for the purpose of measurement, in a state of passionate mind — touching is not a [deliberate] practice.
In looking [at one's semen] — a <s>duṣkṛta</s> (minor wrongdoing).
And in holding [it] downstream or downwind.
No offense — when [emission occurs] suddenly, when engaged in an unrelated activity, by [contact with] thigh, garment, or another's touch, or by scratching.
Of a touch that is not experienced [consciously].

And from mere remembrance [— no offense for] that either.
The classification in [the <s>saṅghāvaśeṣa</s> on] emission.
What is contained in the questions.
When about to fall but not yet fallen — immediately upon entering the excretory channel.
Not by mere commencement is there [the status of] a deliberate practice.
The same — in emission without deliberate practice, in tasting.
Not [an offense] for pressing, rubbing, or massaging the sexual organ.
When this [organ] is serviceable — emission by medicine in the course of treatment.

And another's [semen — the same rules apply].
The question-section on emission.
The adjudicated cases.

children.text: // vinīlikādau vighaṭiti asthiśaṅkalikayoḥ śira<<ḥ>>karṇanāsasu grivānta[11b6]re pārśvapṛṣṭhakroḍavaliṣu vālāntare hastāṃsabāhuṣu bāhvantare kaṭyurupādajaṃ*ghāsu jaṃghāntare ca mocane maulaṃ /
children.translated_text: In [emission by contact with] a bruise and such — [whether] at joints, at bone-connections, at the head, ears, nose, between the neck, at the sides, back, belly, folds [of the body], between the [pubic] hairs, at the hands, shoulders, arms, between the arms, at the hips, thighs, feet, calves, and between the calves — the fundamental [offense applies].

[In emission by contact with] a thick quilt, a forest-mat, an unwoven [fabric], a <s>cilimini</s> [blanket], a <s>bimba</s>-cushion, a pillow, a bed, a stool, a couch-frame, a sitting-board, between seats, a pot, a small pot, a pot-fragment, a basket, a rubbish-heap, stone, plaster, between layers of plaster, a bolt, or pieces of meat.
In pressing a wound.
In pressing [with intent toward] a woman — [it constitutes] a feminine [offense], at the commencement of that [act].
In the insertion of the thumb here.
In emission while approaching [a woman].
And in transferring from place to place.
And of one who reflects unwisely.
Of one who holds the sexual organ.
No offense — from [inadvertent] friction with the bladder [area].
Nor by the embrace of a former second-wife [who is now old].
And in grasping a woman's foot, calf, arm, thigh, or ankle.

The adjudicated cases on emission.
Emission [section] is complete. ||1||
Bodily contact.
What is contained in the <s>vibhaṅga</s>.
A woman is the agent.
Here [i.e., in this context].
In sitting and standing in private.
And in eating together.
In sharing a bed — on a journey, with a woman not recognized as [such] by a man — one who is confused.
In the latter [case] — [the offense pertains] to both.
In teaching a householder's wife — in the presence of a man who is knowledgeable.
Even in his presence — when she is an improper [student].
Of a <s>duṣkṛta</s> (minor wrongdoing) [— it is such].
A lesser [offense] — for one born on an island or of animal nature.
His status as bearer [of the offense].
The other mark [i.e., gender] is useless in that type [of case].
A downward [gesture] here [is the indicator of assent].

children.text: / ājñāne subhaṣita[12a3]durbhāśitayor arthasya trayo n.ye nyatra pratisevane methunasyeti pratibalatve maulasya /
children.translated_text: In ignorance — of the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken [words] — the three [penalties] other than [the prohibition of] sexual intercourse as an attendant — when the fundamental [offense] is in force.
Of the immediate [lesser offense] — elsewhere.
Likewise — a female <s>paṇḍaka</s> (sexually ambiguous person), a male <s>paṇḍaka</s>, and a magically created [woman].
And here, regarding a man — the three [penalties].
If with the desire for experiencing that pleasure — with one who is connected by passion.
In the acceptance of bodily contact.
The same status here — of a bamboo [rod used for touching].
And of a robe connected with that [contact].
No distinction [is made] among — embracing, touching, grasping, seizing, drawing near, rubbing close, marking, and pressing.
And of the use [of any of these].
The immediate [lesser offense] — with a robe as intermediary.
No difference between a <s>duṣkṛta</s> and a lesser [offense].
A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should not be touched.
Nor a [lay]woman.

children.text: / spṛśed aṃbhasyārtām uttāraṇāya bāhau keśeṣu vā mātṛduhitṛbhaginīsaṃjñām upasthāpya /
children.translated_text: One may touch [a woman] who is in danger in water — for the purpose of rescue — at the arm or hair, having established the perception of mother, daughter, or sister.
In a sandy place — for obtaining a sign of life — positioning [her] face-down.
Protecting [her] like a stool [i.e., keeping her stable].
Having assessed the food [needs] — going to cowherds and animal-keepers.
Examining repeatedly — whether [she] is alive or not.
There is no fault in embracing a woman with pure mind, out of compassion.
The classification in [the <s>saṅghāvaśeṣa</s> on] bodily contact.
What is contained in the questions.
A gross [transgression] — when the intention is [to enjoy what is] smooth, warm, and soft.
No offense — in freeing from suffering out of compassion.
Regarding mothers, daughters, and sisters — when that perception [is maintained].
In the greeting of a former companion [now a laywoman].
The question-section in [the <s>saṅghāvaśeṣa</s> on] bodily contact.
The adjudicated cases.
A gross [transgression] — when alms, a dust-clod, or such is thrown into a woman's organ.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> — in striking a woman with the foot-portion and such.
And of its seat [i.e., the surface it occupies].
When lifting up a woman who has slipped and fallen on slippery ground.
No offense when a woman does that three-fold action for him, or when she seizes [him].
In embracing — [only] the measure [of offense applies].
When a daughter sits on one's lap.
When a woman stumbles and falls upon [him].

Adjudicated cases on bodily contact.
Bodily contact [section]. ||2||
Sexual speech.
(a) That pertaining to the <s>vibhaṅga</s>.
In speaking of sexual intercourse.
With a sexual purpose.

children.text: / yatra boddhuṃ bhavyatā sa vijñapane ntaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is the capacity to understand — that one is [counted as] within the addressee.
When something connected with that meaning is spoken — it does not constitute an offense of effort.
There is no distinction among praising, dispraising, requesting, counter-requesting, asking, counter-asking, narrating, suggesting, reviling, and counter-responding.
No offense when the intention is another meaning, or due to a regional dialect.
Or of a name having a similar portion.
The analysis of the [offense of] sexual speech.
(b) That pertaining to questions.

children.text: / sthūlaṃ chekāśīti [12b2]vāde pāpikasīti chekaṃ te pāpakaṃ vā vraṇamukham iti saṃvibhāgaṃ kurviti māṃ saṃvibhajasveti mayā sārdhaṃ svapihi samāgamam vā kurviti /
children.translated_text: A grave offense [arises from saying]: 'You are clever!' or 'It is sinful!' or 'Yours is wicked, that wound-opening!' or 'Make a distribution!' or 'Distribute to me!' or 'Sleep with me, or have union with me!'
Questions on sexual speech.
(c) Adjudicated cases.
In the case of speaking righteously about one who is transforming [magically] in that way.

children.text: / yavān dehi dehi bhagini mahyaṃ yatte bhagini paśyāmi tad dehi yat te bhagini puratas tad dehi yat te bhagini mana-āpaṃ tad dehi priyaṃ te deyam ity aham uktā kin te priyam ity ukte tvaṃ [12b3] me bhagini priyā /
children.translated_text: 'Give barley!' — 'Give, sister, to me!' — 'Sister, let me see what you have!' — 'Give what is before you, sister!' — 'Give, sister, what pleases your mind!' — 'What is dear to you should be given!' — Being told thus, [she asks:] 'What is dear to you?' — [He replies:] 'You, sister, are dear to me!'

children.text: / dehi me bhagini pānīyaṃ khādyakaṃ yavāgūṃ bhojanaṃ tvam evaitad ity uktiṣu /
children.translated_text: In the utterances: 'Give me, sister, water!' — 'food!' — 'gruel!' — 'a meal!' — 'It is you yourself [who must give] this!'
'Donkeys do that to you!'

children.text: / cārikāṃ bhagini carasy ullāpayamānā puruṣān piṇḍapātaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Sister, you go about on your rounds enticing men for alms!'
'A firebrand has been thrown into this one!' — and such.
For one who by nature speaks coarsely — in coarse speaking.
Adjudicated cases on sexual speech.
Go-between activity (<s>sāṃcaritra</s>).
(a) That pertaining to the <s>vibhaṅga</s>.
In praising the attending upon oneself through sexual intercourse.
Likewise, a statement for the purpose of approving what has been thus praised.
The counter-utterance of that very [praise].
When there is no connection with that sexual intercourse — it constitutes an offense of effort.
Of that [go-between activity] by both.
The praising of service.
In the union.
Of another.
Through another.
For that purpose.

children.text: / anupanatopanateḥ sampatyeḥ gṛhītadauteyasya saṃprayojyato nivedi bhavatas tatretaratadukte pūrvatra pravedane /
children.translated_text: From the approaching of one not approached, from the coming together, from the seizure of a messenger, from the employing [of someone] — having reported at the other [party's location], when the other states that [here, the first has been informed].
The completion [of the offense is] when it is heard, even without personal intervention.
The separateness of these [steps] in what must be done.
When the last [step] is not done, when [the agent] is not present — there is no offense of effort.
When it is not fruitful — even though the counter-agent's task is complete — there is no loss of the undertaking.
The self-agency here belongs to the messenger.
The employing-agency [belongs to] his master.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> (minor offense) for another.
The status of being speech includes written [messages], hand [signals], overhead pointing, and appointed signs at meeting-places.
The approaching [of the woman means] the status of being a courtesan.
And the prostituting, without ownership, prior to the four [meetings].
The failure [of the arrangement] — when there is benefit of the result.

children.text: / tadvaśā ced abhāryānuśrāvitatve prāṇivattvaṃ tadantarasamantarakalihitatvatilintilikācchinnatvatrisaṅkarāparitatvācārapratiniḥsṛṣṭatvābhāryānuśrāvitatvaghaṇṭā ca ghuṣṭatvānāṃ duḥkritakṛttvaṃ trayasyāsyām āryasya /
children.translated_text: If by that [failure's] power — when what is not a wife is heard of: the living-being status, the intimate-licking between them, the cutting off of the <s>tilintilika</s> (parasitic worm), the not being encompassed by the three-fold mixing, the being released by proper conduct, the being heard of as not a wife, and the proclamation with a bell — a <s>duṣkṛta</s> for the noble one in three [of these cases].

children.text: / kasmād ayaṃ na pratitiṣṭhatīyaṃ na gacchati śvaśuragṛhān na nīyata iti coktīnāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Why does this one not settle?' — 'Why does this one not go [to the husband's house]?' — 'Why is she not taken to the in-laws' house?' — and [such] utterances.
The analysis of the go-between [offense].
(b) That pertaining to questions.
A grave offense in go-between [activity involving] desire, falling into [temptation], practice, play, and approaching on one's own behalf.
In the designation — when one is settled [in the arrangement].
In carrying off by quarrel.
When told: 'Buy such-and-such a woman as a wife!'
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> [for saying merely] 'a woman.'
'Some [woman] may be obtained' — and such.
Questions on go-between [activity].
(c) Adjudicated cases.
A grave offense for one who has given — by the arrangement without reconciliation.
By calling out, making a <s>dharma</s>-pretext the precedent.

.
Go-between [activity]. ||4||

Faultlessness of the procession of the four postures — during this journey.
The non-authoritativeness [applies] to both the commissioned and the non-commissioned.
Self-agency [belongs to] the commissioned one.

children.text: / pratīṣṭā vaḥ yathoktakāre kāyena vā vācā vā /
children.translated_text: 'Let there be your acceptance of what is done as stated — either by body or by speech.'
The oneness of the act.
The non-agency of the limbs [applies when there is] a difference [in parties].
When requested or permitted by him — when the substance is not examined by one such as him
— when the location of the dwelling is not indicated — at the end of the proceeding.
Even in the subsequent [act] — this [applies when it is] unrequested.
When [the building is] of excessive measure, for one purpose.
Unfittingness, disturbance, and non-retreat — [these constitute] impurity [of the site].

children.text: / kṣudrajantvāśayavattvaṃ rājakulatīrthakāvasathasanniḥsṛtatvāc chedyavṛkṣatvam arvāgvyāmāntānantaryato bahirnadīprāgbhārodapānāvaṣṭabdhatvam iti yathāsaṃkhyam etāni /
children.translated_text: Having small creatures' habitation; being an outlet from a royal court, <s>tīrthika</s> settlement, or rest-house; having trees that must be cut; being within a <s>vyāma</s>'s distance without interval from a river; and being propped up with a water-supply from the east — these [impurities], respectively.
The standard measure is one and a half hands, being the <s>Sugata</s>'s span.
From that, twelve [spans] by seven — the interior measurement.
Having obtained the designation from the <s>Saṃgha</s> — the designated status.
One whose [site] is impure should not request [permission].

children.text: / svapratyayena vā gaccheyu niyuktānāṃ vā bhikṣūṇām /
children.translated_text: Or one should go by one's own authority, or [with the authority] of commissioned monks.
This applies also to the bedding [arrangement].
No offense for what has been acquired and enjoyed.
And in the renovation of an old [building].
Hut — <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> — for the <s>Saṃgha's</s> purpose. Monastery — <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>.
(b) That pertaining to questions.
The offense of effort [arises from] the beginning [of construction].
Likewise, within [the section on] uncovered cause.
For multiple purposes — when not released by the individual.
And of one who has been wronged.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> when there is no completion, after the requesting.
Questions pertaining to the hut and monastery <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>. ||5||
The <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> of groundless [accusation].

children.translated_text: Of a monk [accused of] conduct leading to a <s>pārājika</s> offense — even of one who is destroyed — here from [mere] partisanship, self-agency through false statement, in a communication to someone.
With the desire to undermine.
That basis is not intermediate.
When one who has been confused has the non-existence [of the basis] — in the case of groundless false speech — the meaning-essence [is relevant].

In the censure based on a different portion.
Falsely, by a statement established through another pretext.

The groundless contentiousness.
A grave offense in censure without the [actual] practice.
And when the name is not supported.

children.translated_text: In the case of slandering regarding drawing blood from a <s>Tathāgata</s> with malicious intent and splitting the <s>Saṃgha</s> — saying 'this was spoken with an ulterior motive' — even this is a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
Questions on groundless contentiousness. ||8||
On <s>Saṃgha</s>-splitting.
A grave offense when drawing away to another assembly.
Non-compliance in the form of non-relinquishment and non-performance — in the form of prohibition.
The prohibition-status of the announcement; the single-moment character of the statement.
The separateness of the turning [from the offense].
Not of the conclusion.
The offense of effort [arises from] the undertaking.
Of one for whom banishment-censure-reminder has not been performed.
This should not be proclaimed.

children.text: / naiṣu na nājñapayeyur methakena karmaṇā ca /
children.translated_text: Among those, one should not not proclaim — by mutual action.
At its end — upon relinquishment.
Of the one who has retreated.
In the split.
Of the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
The <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> of <s>Saṃgha</s>-splitting. ||9||
On following [the schismatic].
Of one who assumes the supporting role of that [schismatic].
The following — <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>. ||10||
On corrupting families.

children.text: / svapravāsanasya kartari saṃghe mithyāśāyenaiṣāsyātra pravṛttir iti vaktṛtvasya mṛṣā /
children.translated_text: Of the performer of one's own banishment — in the <s>Saṃgha</s> — falsely assuming the role of speaker [to say]: 'This [banishment] has been undertaken with a wrong intention.'
The <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> of corrupting families. ||11||
On intractability.

children.text: / coditatve bhikṣuṇādhiśīlam avacanīyatvasyātra bhikṣubhir ātmanaḥ kṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: When censured by a monk regarding the higher training — the self-agency here, of the monks, is [in declaring] his being beyond reproach.

The <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> of intractability. ||12||
The <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> [offenses] are complete.

On [the offense regarding] keeping [robes beyond the allotted time].
On the first day-and-night — this [robe] does not have existence [as an offense object].
In effort, vessel-possession, and dwelling.
The first dawn is the beginning of this.
At sunrise — the action [becomes final] by completion.
The existence of a <s>naissargika</s> [offense arises] primarily from awareness.
Its departure when it has been transferred [to another].
Its existence [applies] when the regulation is for the purpose of ordination.
And in the allocation of a robe.
The destruction of its following for three [days].
And in the loss of the fundamental [status].
When [the robe] exists, even elsewhere — the arising [of the offense applies] regarding that thing.
When arising, in the seven-day [period].
The <s>naissargika</s> character — when that offense exists — in a mere requisite that has been accepted.
This does not [apply] when a section [of the robe] is deficient.
Nor for communal [property].
Discharge [from the offense] is the authoritative rule here.
This threefold [rule] does not [apply to] one who has spread the <s>kaṭhina</s> [robe].
When the self-agency of one who has followed [the rule] exists — ten nights.
Beginning from the next day.
In the [case of the] dwelling-robe.
Three circles — the measure from the covering-edge to the extremity.
When not connected by determination.

children.text: / [13b5] sambaddhe ca sānuvṛttau anyatrānadhiṣṭhitatadgotrāt prabhṛty anyatra /
children.translated_text: And when connected — with following — except from an undetermined [robe] of that class, and except from another [class].
The <s>naissargika</s> of keeping [robes]. ||1||
On separation [from robes].
(a) That pertaining to the <s>vibhaṅga</s>.
Faultless is separation by one night's stay.

children.text: / na pramīlya pratyāstaraṇaṃ gacchen na ced anyaiva pratiprāptir iti saṃsthā /
children.translated_text: One should not go to sleep closing one's eyes, [thinking:] 'I shall not reach the covering' — unless there is certainly another [way of] attaining [it] — this is the rule.

children.text: / vāse devam abhipretya gato kālasampattau tatra yācitvaitat* /
children.translated_text: When one has gone intending a robe-observance at a monastery — if the season is appropriate — this should be requested there.
When inappropriate — [one should use] a four-fold upper-robe, keeping vigil for the greater part [of the night].
In an unworthy [dwelling] — when the outer robe has been deposited — one should deposit the rains-season robe in the dwelling.
Not in rain.
Not when what must be crossed is between rivers.
Not when there is apprehension of either [flood or rain].

children.text: / sabhikṣukasakapāṭakatvaṃ* sāhitam āvāsyavarṣattā devasya varṣāśaṅkitā vā jalāntaritatvaṃ gantavyasyety asyābhāvenādattasamvṛttir aṇāstīrṇakaṭhinaḥ saṃghāṭīṃ* vinā na kvacid* gacchet* /
children.translated_text: Having a monk, having shutters — when combined — the dwelling-place, the rains-season of the monastery, or apprehension of rain, or the crossing-place being water-separated — in the absence of these — having not taken [the robe], one who has not spread the <s>kaṭhina</s> should not go anywhere without the outer robe.
When there is impossibility of obtaining another designated robe-place — abandoning [the previous] designation — a counter-measure.

children.text: / dānam avipravāsasaṃvṛtteḥ saṃghāṭyā gurukatve jīrṇaṃ vādhikayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The giving of the outer-robe, [regarded] as heavy, when the arrangement of non-separation is [established] — or the worn-out [robe] of the two [that remain], when excessive.
The agency of one whose designated [robe] has not obtained the arrangement.
When the dawn rises while one is in a place other than the place [of the robe] with its adjacent area.
When a boundary is established — the limit is the boundary-place.
When unified — there is no breaking of the sub-boundaries by the one who has circumscribed.
And when undivided — in terms of property and in terms of view.
When branches and sub-branches are not touching — the separate standing of the common root.
And of root, non-root, and so on.
Of trees with touching branches and canopy — single standing.
Like a terrace — the entry of the lower portion therein.
And of a boat and a cart.
When without boundary — the limit is the extent of the encompassed limb.
The adjacent-area span measured by the surrounding space.

children.text: / kuḍyaparikṣipto grāme yāvat ṣaḍgavayuktena vaṃśaśakaṭena[14a3] sphuraṇam adhvanā vā kukkuṭasyotpātya nilayane vāṭaparikṣipte jaiḍakarajāsaṃprakṛtihrīmatpuruṣapravicārabhūmyadhvanā vā /
children.translated_text: In a village enclosed by a wall — as far as a bamboo cart yoked with six oxen can turn, or by the road — or the flight of a rooster [rising] to alight, or in an enclosure surrounded by a fence — the roaming-ground of a modest man of the <s>jaiḍaka</s>-<s>rāja</s> (<s>Jaiḍaka</s> king's) disposition, or by the road.
In [a village] enclosed by a moat — by a staircase of twelve steps, or the road [measured by] refuse-heap, thick clod [throwing distance].

children.text: / tatsthāne trikaraṇīyaparisarpaṇātinā mana rajobhiś ca yāvatas tadagatasya saṃbhāvanaṃ /
children.translated_text: At that place — through the three actions of creeping forward, and by dust-particles — the estimation [of the offense] for as many as have reached that [place].
On a road without a boundary, for a human being of uninterrupted movement — forty-nine bow-lengths.

children.text: / na sīmāntaraṃ pṛthaktvaṃ krośāntān madhyataḥ parasya /
children.translated_text: Not the separateness of another boundary — from the end of a <s>krośa</s>, of the middle [area] from the other.
// The analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>) in the <s>naiḥsargika</s> of dwelling apart //
(a) That which pertains to miscellaneous [rules](?)
Not [an offense] when a portion of the evil [area] is approached — of what is designated [as permissible].
Not [an offense] regarding non-completion in the <s>naiḥsargika</s>.
And in [the case of property] belonging to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
From this, dwelling apart [occurs].
Not [a loss of] the other location's status from [its being under] another's designation.
Not this of the two — <s>Dharma</s>-body — if from [a different] viewpoint, there is no charge.
[14a5] Not with shared [property] — of a vestibule.
Not 'by wealth' — thus, of father and son.
Even [when] excluded — this [rule applies].
And in [the case of] eating together.
There should be no inspection-status in a village — when a monastery does not exist.
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> of dwelling apart // 2 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,3) On the monthly [robe].
(a) What is contained in the analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>).

children.text: / pūrṇavadasatyāṃ pūrakapratyāsāṃ māṃ nyūnaṃ māṃ samasāmantakāt* /
children.translated_text: When full [i.e., complete] — in the absence of a supplementary [robe], a lesser [one]; neither less nor equal — from the vicinity.
And when there is [a question of] what is to be designated — for the sentient being.
Elsewhere, when thirty days have been exceeded for this [robe].
[14a6] The non-supplementary character of a different kind [of cloth] — from the color and so forth.
All colors [are permissible] in whiteness [i.e., undyed cloth].
When its group-[counting] and so forth are established — in the fulfillment of that [requirement].
Two layers from uncut [cloth] — up to the outer robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>).
And of the sitting-mat.
Single [layer] — the upper robe (<s>uttarāsaṅga</s>) and the under-garment (<s>antarvāsana</s>).
Double — from uncut [cloth that is] seasonal.
No restriction regarding those made of rags.
One should give additional [pieces] when there is insufficiency in a tattered [robe] — as much as needed.
The non-give-ability of the excess.
And its <s>naiḥsargika</s> (forfeiture) character.

children.text: / na nyāyyam utpāṭayed atraiva parikarma kṛtvāropayiṣya ity anusampādya cittaṃ /
children.translated_text: It is not proper to uproot [stitching] with the thought 'I shall perform repairs right here and reattach' — having prepared the mind.
Of what has been uprooted as it was — from the prior conjunction, the <s>naiḥsargika</s> character [arises].
In a patched outer robe — from the ninth [patch] onward, from twenty-five [patches], excluding pairs.
Beyond that — a quilt.
In the first of these — by groups of three, the state of having two or three circles [of patches].
Three-and-a-half circles in the second.
In the third — the state of four-and-a-half circles.
Three [sets of] five, by one's own hands — the largest [are] the designated ones.
The smallest — releasing half a hand-span on both sides.
The measure of the middle ones [lies] in between.
Of the under-garment — also two [sets of] five, and also two [sets of] four.
Even from the state of covering up to three circles.
Two-sevenths of the body — the meaning of 'hand-span.'
When one does not have it made — the making of a granary [fold].
// [14b3] The analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>) of the monthly <s>naiḥsargika</s> //
(b) What pertains to questions.
The character of a <s>duṣkṛta</s> — like [that of a] lesser [offense] — in the intermediate [period].
The non-expectancy of half a circle in covering.
And in what is improper.
And of those without designation — face-cloth, wiping-cloth, straining-cloth, floor-covering, eyelid-covering, and such — the ancillary robes.

// The questions on the monthly [<s>naiḥsargika</s>] //
// The monthly <s>naiḥsargika</s> // 3 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,4) On washing.
(a) What is contained in the analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>).
Staying inside for the purpose of protection [of modesty].
Non-watching by <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> in this [matter].
[14b4] Giving of alms-food to this [person] [who is washing].
A relative — one who is a first predecessor through either one of the parents up to the seventh [generation].
The agency of the recognition [of kinship] is by priority. In a group — that [same principle applies].
Of the two [conditions]: being a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, and not being a relative of that [person].
And in the subsequent [rule].
Of the designated [items] — one's own old robes worthy of washing, and sitting-mats — for whom [is] the washing, dyeing, and beating [to be done] — by request.
Even when only a portion has been done — the act is considered done.
When done, the character of having been caused to be done [also applies].
[14b5] Unity [of the act extends] up to the completion of the result.
When [the results] have the nature of [successive] stages — unity of the results.
When recognition is predominant — the root [offense applies] according to the actual meaning.
The status of a secondary [offense] when [the recognition] is not according to actual meaning — [the decision rests with] one who has doubt, like one who has recognition.
One should guard <s>Saṃgha</s>-property [used in] the act.

children.text: / anissaraṇam atrāgantukatvaṃ sadasatvarūpanirjñānārtham asya tena praśnaḥ /
children.translated_text: Non-departure here — the character of being a newcomer; the question by him for the purpose of ascertaining the form, whether it exists or not.
[text damaged/illegible]
No disturbance from <s>Saṃgha</s> [property] that the <s>Buddha</s> has spoken of.

children.text: / gṛhṇīyān niḥsṛ[15a1] / / jyamānam atirekaṃ pātracīva<<ra>>śikyasaritakāyabandhanaṃ saṃgha upanikṣepāya /
children.translated_text: [15a1] One should take the surplus being released — [the objects of] bowl, robe, hanging-strap, carrying-cord, and body-band — as a deposit for the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
Likewise [it is] a deposit for him; taking [it back] as one wishes, with its substitutes.
// The analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>) in the <s>naiḥsargika</s> on washing //
(b) What pertains to questions.
No diminishment [of the offense] when washing what is soiled with urine, excrement, drain-water, mud, and the like.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> — for eyelid-coverings, house-cloths, pillows, [cloths that have been] allocated, released, and those belonging to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

// [15a2] The questions on the <s>naiḥsargika</s> on washing //
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on washing // 4 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,5) On receiving [robes from <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>].
(a) What is contained in the analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>).

children.text: / pratigṛhṇīyād bhikṣuṇī mahārhaṃ vāsaḥ parivarhaṇāya kuryād bhikṣuṇyā sārddhaṃ parivarttaṃ /
children.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should receive a valuable garment for the purpose of exchange; she should make an exchange together with a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>.
Or with an equal [value garment], satisfying her thereby.
// On receiving.
Of a robe by request.
No offense in giving a bolt of cloth to the <s>Saṃgha</s> — of a friendly [gift].
Of one who is to be fully ordained — of two who have been dwelling [together].

children.text: / cittaśraddham udbhāvya purataḥ sthāpayitva nira[15a3]pekṣaṇaṃ prakramaṇe
children.translated_text: Having aroused faith of mind, having placed [the offering] before [the monk], disregard [is proper] in proceeding [without taking it].
// The analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>) in the <s>naiḥsargika</s> on receiving //
(b) What pertains to questions.
The state of being like an elephant — for one who has received.
Seeing, inspection, reaching that [state], and so forth — the character of an attempt, when the standing [position] is not present.
The clarity and the character of being a traveler's requisite — the system in giving a bolt of cloth and the like.
No offense — for the time being, with a temporal mind, when one forgets to take the price.

// The questions on the <s>naiḥsargika</s> on receiving //
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on receiving // 5 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,6) The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on requesting.
One who has gone to the human destiny, who has become a householder, who is a living being not a relative — [requesting from such a one is] offense-producing.
And in the subsequent three [cases].
When robes have not been stolen, lost, burned, or carried away — of one who has [only] half a robe.
In the request — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
In obtaining the root [offense applies] — of a robe.
Of one who is not deficient [in robes].
The request [should be] of whatever kind — equal in value and color.
No offense for [requesting] another [kind].
And no [offense in] requesting from a <s>tuka</s> and a group of ten.
And the lesser [offense] of one's own place.
Likewise, its nature [applies].
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on requesting // 6 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,7) One who is eligible to be requested [for robes].
In the absence of all designated [robes] — the eligibility to be requested.
The nature of the offense for this.

children.text: / paraṃ gṛhiṇo dvādaśahastakaḥ paḍakottaram antaraṃ saptadvikaṣāṭakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The limit for a householder — twelve hand-spans; the upper [limit for] a bolt is an interval of seven pairs of cloth-pieces.
For a <s>bhikṣu</s> — in the largest [size], with the stated number of layers, the outer robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>) and under-garment.
The pair [of robes] may be requested.
Either one of them.
What is in excess of this measure — may not be requested.

children.text: / pūrvakasya ca pūrvalabdhau uttaralabdhāv adhikasya deyatvaṃ /
children.translated_text: And of the former [robe] — when what was obtained first [is still available], [but] a superior one has been obtained — the excess should be given away.
The excess from a later acquisition should be given away.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> — when what should not be requested is requested.
15a5r
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> — when what should not be requested is requested.
In obtaining — the root [offense].
And in not giving what should be given.
// [15b1] The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on eligibility to request // 7 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,8) The designated [offering].
What is designated [for one], of one who has not been excluded — known [as] equal to what is not designated.
That itself is something other.
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on designated solicitation // 8 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,9) Each individually.
The clarity [should pertain] to the giver.
Unity of what is obtained — in the unity of the attempt.
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on individual [solicitation] // 9 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,10) What is sent.

children.text: / preṣitam akalpikaṃ cīvaramūlyaṃ pratikṣipya paripraṣṇapūrvakam upadiṣṭaṃ vaiyāpṛtyakaram ādiṣṭaṃ dūtenokto vṛttā[15b2]ntātvākhyānapūrvakañ codayeta /
children.translated_text: Having rejected the sent, improper robe-price, one should urge — having first asked questions, instructed the steward, directed the messenger, having first reported the event — [one should] urge [compliance].
When there is inability — the character of having been urged through deliberation.
If [there is] no result — a second [urging] too.
And a third.
After that — one should stand in designation up to the third [time].
If [there is] no result — one should inform the donor.

children.text: / vṛttāyām evaṃ pratiniḥśriṣṭau prayacchata uktapratiniḥsargād abhyupetadātṛcittagrahaṇānuṣṭhānāt pratigṛhṇīyāt* /
children.translated_text: When [the process] has occurred — thus, in the relinquishment, when the donor gives [it] — from the stated relinquishment, from the performance of accepting the mind of the agreed-upon donor — one should accept.
Or by further urging — when [the steward] has agreed to the arrangement.
When [it is] taken.
And when two or three human [messengers] have taken it.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> — when not stated.
When not rejected.
And when instruction is given without being asked.
And in disappointment — in informing.
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on what is sent // 10 //
(a) What is contained in the analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>).
One should keep a mattress [made of silk].
Of both the making and the reason [for it].
Of silk (<s>kauśeya</s>).
The state of being spread out and such — in a mattress.
Of one whose making is completed.
No offense — [15b4] in obtaining for enjoyment and embellishment.
// The analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>) in the <s>naiḥsargika</s> on silk //
(b) What pertains to questions.
The lesser [offense applies] when mixed with lesser [amounts of silk].
And when the substance has perished.
// The questions on the <s>naiḥsargika</s> on silk // 11 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,12) On pure black [wool].
Of the wool of pure black rams.
By birth [i.e., natural color].
The applicability [extends] to [those of] the <s>nīla</s> (blue), <s>karṇa</s> (ear-colored), <s>makara</s>, <s>kañca</s>, and <s>śaka</s> [breeds].
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on pure black [wool] // 12 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,13) The two-part [proportion].
When there is excess — half of those [should be of another color].
[15b5] Equal portions of the remaining [colors] — of [wool from] pastured, open-range goats.
From the side, back, and neck [of the animal] — the first [category].
From the head, feet, and belly — the latter [category].
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on the two-part [proportion] // 13 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,14) The six-year [rule].
When length or hand-span is excessive — cutting.
Increasing when [it is] short or does not cover.
In cutting — joining [the pieces].
Repair — when [there is] breakage or weakness.
When [it is] beyond repair — giving [it away].

children.text: / alabdhasamvṛtteḥ saty anyatra svakām atyakte vāna<<ti>>krānte /
children.translated_text: Of one who has not obtained a replacement — when it exists elsewhere, or when one's own has not been abandoned and has not exceeded [the time limit].
[16a1] When six years have passed — the state of having been fulfilled — of the mattress.
Like [the killing of] a sentient being — the transgression [occurs] at the commencement.
Not at the final [stage] — the non-offense character of the attempt.
The separateness of one [who goes forth under] another ordination.
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on six years // 14 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,15) The hand-span [sitting-mat].
In the use of a new sitting-mat without having given up the old one, not designated, the <s>Sugata</s>-hand-span — with those [measurements].
If this [condition is met].
Even by this much.
Even when repair is possible.
[16a2] Or by the gathering of materials.
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on the hand-span [sitting-mat] // 15 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,16) Carrying wool.
When there is and is not a carrier — carrying ram's or sheep's wool beyond three <s>yojanas</s>.
A <s>krośa</s> is the essence of audible movement.

children.text: / prayogasyārddhaṃ duṣkṛtam ṛddher anyena nabhasā haraṇe nirmite ca /
children.translated_text: Half of the attempt [constitutes] a <s>duṣkṛta</s> — in carrying by supernatural power, by another, through the sky, or by a magically created [being].
Freedom from fault — for a sheath, a bundle, a plaster, a body-cover, a lump of clay, a ball, and <s>murucikā</s> — [being] without purpose — of just that measure.

Of paramāṇu (ultimate atom), atom, block, copper-weight, hare[-foot], cow[-foot], window-opening, dust-mote, nit, louse, barley-grain, finger — six [of each make up] the former [measure, which becomes] the next.

children.text: / ṣaṭ caturaṅgulo hasto rdhacaturtha<<ḥ>> hastakaḥ puruṣaś ca caturhastakaṃ dhanus tat śatapañcakaṃ krośaḥ /
children.translated_text: Six [finger-breadths make] four <s>aṅgulas</s>, [which equal] a hand; three-and-a-half hands [make] a hand-span; and four hand-spans [make] a man[-length]; [one] bow[-length equals that]; five hundred of those [make] a <s>krośa</s>.
From the end of that onward — of what is to be carried — one should not bear the body's burden.
Not on the sides, back, hip, or head.
In this [matter], what is not to be suspected is its non-shareable nature.
One should not uproot more than half.
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on carrying wool // 16
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,17) Processing wool.
In place of an old non-robe [item] — sheep's wool.
Carding — in place of beating.
// The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on processing wool // 17 //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,3,18) On gold and silver.
When a precious thing has been accepted [as one's own].
When [the acceptance] is current — its fulfillment [constitutes the offense].
And of one's own [gold/silver] that has not been rendered proper.
And touched — by touching.
In whatever way.
Of a bowl-[shaped vessel of] copper — a <s>duṣkṛta</s> (minor wrongdoing).
No offense — for another [type of vessel].
Of tin, lead-tin, tin-lead, and iron — and for the two novices.

children.text: / [16a5] dānapateḥ svāmitvādhimokṣo vaiyyapṛtyakarasya svāmitvādhimokṣo vaiyāpṛtyākarasya svāmitvābhyupagamanamaidhiṣṭhānam iti kalpāḥ /
children.translated_text: The donor's assumption of ownership, the steward's assumption of ownership, the steward's acceptance of ownership, and the formal authorization — these are the allowable [procedures].
No customary use [is permitted] except from a cause pertaining to the non-existent <s>Dharma</s>-purpose.
When the owner is far away — no destruction [of ownership occurs].
Cooking food for one's own use is allowable.
And the acceptance of a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (coin) for the purpose of handing over to the steward.
And from the non-going of wholesome food.
One who desires fire should prepare a sun-stone [crystal for kindling].
One should not leave it unguarded.
One should not show it to a taker of the given and not-given.
One should give to him the fruit of what is produced.
One who desires water — a moon-stone.
The rule of maintenance is the same.
There is no [offense of] unauthorized acceptance when permission for repair of a jewel is [granted].
One should not accept a vessel of brass, bronze, bell-metal, or wood.
If there is use of this [improper vessel] or another that has been accepted — [it is permissible only] with the use of a medicine-dish.
Two [types] are proper for formal authorization — iron and earthenware.
Jewels (<s>ratna</s>) [include]: gems, pearls, beryl, conch-shell, crystal, coral, silver, gold, [stones] with a stone-core, emerald, red-stone, dextral-spiral [conch], and such.
A lesser [offense] — for a non-traveler.
And for the immediately [next category].
This [includes] what is: cut, broken, in fragments, burnt, previously uncirculated, unwoven, unmarked, or counterfeit.
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> (forfeiture offense) on gold and silver. ||18||
Currency transactions.
Upon receiving — the arising of the offense.
When taken by another without knowledge — the fundamental [offense applies].
Upon the arising of increase.
And for the immediately [subsequent].
From transaction by money or by jewel.
Unity in application.
One may employ [it] for the purpose of [obtaining] jewels.
When there are a monastery-attendant and a lay-follower — by appointment.

children.text: / bandhakaṃ dviguṇam ādāya sākṣisamvatsaraṃ āsadivasasaṃghasthavirovārika gṛhītṛdhanalā[16b4]bhānāropya patre /
children.translated_text: Taking the bond-document doubled, [recording] the witness, the year, the day, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>-elder or deputy-elder, having written [the amount of] the wealth received — on a document.
Having become aware of this — one should report [it] to the other [party].
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on currency transactions. ||19||
Buying and selling.

children.text: / anyena dadyāt sāṃghikaṃ saṃghabhaktopakrīṇate dhānyaṃ mūlyena /
children.translated_text: Through another, one should give <s>Saṅgha</s> [property]; the <s>Saṅgha</s> purchases grain for communal meals with [its own] funds.
If [from] that same [donor] — with a surplus.
The <s>Saṅgha</s> should buy when there is a deficiency.
And new [supplies].
Having sold old [supplies] — if they are without value.
One should not fix a price.
One should not thrust one's hand into householder transactions.
The purchasing [should be done] by a householder.
When there is no supply — [one should] extract from a guarantee or by adjudication.

children.text: / akaraṇaṃ parārthe py utsṛjya ratnatrayaṃ paṇāpaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not doing even for another's sake — setting aside the Three Jewels — [constitutes] a market transaction.
One should not make a bond-contract.
By the <s>Saṅgha</s>, for that purpose — giving through a <s>Saṅgha</s>-officer, designating [the recipient].
One should not undertake [transactions] for the <s>Saṅgha's</s> benefit without asking the most senior elders.
Where [amounts are] recorded — one should follow through on that supply.
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on buying and selling. ||20||
Bowl-retention.
Of a bowl that has been formally authorized.
Its being released — when one is restrained for the purpose of concern about ordination.
The impropriety of [bowls that are] excessively pale, white, or deficient — and also of one below [the minimum] measure.
The faultlessness of a single improper bowl.
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on bowl-retention. ||21||
Bowl-exchange.

children.text: / nādhilobhaṃ kurvīt pariskāre tyadhyāvasānaṃ na patrād astadhāyet* /
children.translated_text: One should not be excessively greedy regarding requisites; one should not renounce [the use of the bowl]; one should not put aside the bowl.
One should request a bowl even when there is none [available].
When one exists.
Up to four bindings — [a bowl] worthy of that.
In the use of what is serviceable.
In exchange — one obtained by solicitation is known.
This [applies] also in the subsequent [case] — for both.
Among third [parties] — and in other cases.
No fault — and the one unknown, of the growth-bowl, is of the knower [— no offense].
The fundamental [offense is] a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
Then, in the [resulting] surplus.
Abandonment — when there is an approved residence.
With one's own requisites — when they exist — of these.
In exchange — with the consent of the senior.
Its forfeiture to the <s>Saṅgha</s>.
When one [person has] many — of the most desired.
Another's should be employed.
This [applies] in the case of ordination.
The giving of an inferior [bowl] to him.
The extraction [is done] by circulation.
By formal [procedure].
When he will do [the exchange] tomorrow — the announcement by that one.

children.text: saṃghe sāmagrivelāyāṃ śvo 'ham āyusmanta unna<<taṃ>> pātraṃ cārayiṣyāmi yusmābhiḥ svakasvakāni pātrāṇi gṛhītvā saṃghamadhye vataritavyam iti /
children.translated_text: 'In the <s>Saṅgha</s>, at the time of harmony — tomorrow I, the venerable one, shall circulate the bowl that has been raised. You should take your own respective bowls and descend into the midst of the <s>Saṅgha</s>.'
The procedure for the purpose of formal session.
Announcement, approach, and offering.

children.text: / sthavi[17a4]redaṃ <<pātraṃ>> svacchaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ paribhogakṣamaṃ sa ced ākāṃkṣasi gṛhāṇeti yathā guṇaṃ rucyā grahaṇaṃ ayācanaṃ gṛhitasyāntaritena /
children.translated_text: 'Elder — this bowl is clean, well-rounded, and fit for use; if you desire it, take it' — thus, according to quality, acceptance by preference — not by solicitation; when what has been accepted is superseded.
When there is non-giving of both — the report of the one who has obtained the voice of the other, the one not formally authorized for both.
Its employment — slowly and gradually, without breaking.
Transacting with this one — by both [parties].
Here, the separation of the better [bowl] — of the subsidiary one.
Of the lighter — the [risk of] breakage.
Not at all in [its] status as an eating-vessel.
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on bowl-exchange.
Weaving [i.e., having robes woven].
Without price — in having [a robe] woven by another through solicitation.
Not [an offense] when [the request is] continuous and not done for that [inappropriate purpose].
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on weaving. ||23||
Increasing what is being prepared [i.e., upgrading a robe being woven].
That [robe] is designated — of the drink [offering associated with it].

children.text: / bhūyas tāyāṃ vā durniyogataḥ sauṣṭhave vā /
children.translated_text: When there is excess — or from misappropriation, or for propriety.
If there is a deficiency — [the liability falls on] the giver.
Non-giving — [the liability falls on] the decision-maker.
When those who have not given permission [claim] that it is the giver's purpose — regarding the agent.
Upon the accomplishment of the fundamental [purpose].
The practice of the previously understood designated [offering] — of the <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
The truth of the approach of one who has not been restrained.
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on increasing what is being prepared. ||24||
Confiscation.
The <s>bhikṣu</s>-status of one to be separated.
The non-self-made status of what is to be confiscated.
Its status as a robe.

children.text: / samastayor vyastayor vā kāyavācor āchedārthaṃ pravṛttis tasya /
children.translated_text: The proceeding for the purpose of confiscation — by body, speech, or both, jointly or separately.
And of one appointed for that — regarding the agent.
Of the last — upon completion, the separation from the body.
In [deliberate] effort — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
The obligation to return it.
Self-interest is not a constituent here.
Like extraction — for one not fully ordained.
Here, the obstruction of confiscation — of one whose self-attainment has not materialized.
The unsuitability of what is done without authorization.
An offense — from one who acts harmfully and purposelessly, for the purpose of obstructing activity.
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on confiscation. ||25||
The six-night [rule].
Like one's own place — when there is danger, for the forest-dweller — the [taking of only] one robe into the village.
One may dwell away from that — which has gone inside a house — by compulsion of circumstance, up to the sixth day.
[The offense is] obstructed if [mindfulness is] not relaxed.
No fault — when arrival [is prevented] by compulsion of an obstacle.
Not a constituent here — when the six-night [period] is being traversed, the intention at departure.
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on dwelling away for six nights. ||26||
The rains-robe (<s>varṣāśāṭī</s>).
From the day of one's own admission forward — from the <s>āsāḍī</s> [full moon] onward, one should seek the rains-robe.
One should retain it until a fortnight after one's own rains-[retreat ends].
The agency [of offense] — for the earlier and later periods from this.
In the retention of one obtained for the first time by another — exchange [with a] <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
Of the last — upon accomplishment.
A lesser [offense] — when [the robe] is dissolved [i.e., worn out].
According to the manner of admission — that which follows it.
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on the rains-robe. ||27||
The urgent [distribution].
The agency — of the rains-[retreat] gain.
When accepted within the rains-[retreat].
Having set aside — at the end, by compulsion of urgency, within ten days — of what is obtainable.
And when it has been distributed — of this also.
And when it has not been distributed.
Without [distribution] — subjection to the donor's statement.
In the immediate [subsequent period] — by compulsion of the <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony) and such, on a day — of the unauthorized custodians.
They should not disregard him.
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on urgent [distribution]. ||28||
Diversion [of offerings].

children.text: // pudgale nyatra saṃghe vā saṃkalpitasyānyena cīvarasya [18a1] jānatātmani pariṇāmato labdhau /
children.translated_text: When a robe designated for a [specific] individual other than the <s>Saṅgha</s> — by another, knowingly diverted to oneself — upon receiving [it].
In the diversion — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
And here — for the other [party].
And of its result.
And of the other [party].
When there is non-sentient [or] non-countable status — of the one to be separated and the one to be joined.
And when [it is] only a partial [diversion].
No offense — when there is no receipt, in the case of seeking [food] scraps for animals and such.

children.text: / kalpate yā cchayā pratinidhyantare sugatasya dānam /
children.translated_text: It is allowable — that which, by whose shadow, as a substitute, is given to the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha).
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> — in the intentional taking.
Going beyond the boundary — in the formal authorization of <s>Saṅgha</s> [property].
In distribution by those who are distracted.
Without formal authorization.

children.text: / ekasya dvayoḥ trayāṇāṃ vā saṃghādā bhavato lābhasyādāne /
children.translated_text: In the taking by one, two, or three of gain that comes from the <s>Saṅgha</s>.
By this procedure — the shareholder-status of others.
The status of stealing — with a thieving mind.
One should not suddenly render the <s>vihāra</s> without residents.
In giving to the obedient one — there, after inspection.
When [the robe] does not arrive — bowing down for ten years.
With five [daily portions of] alms-food.

children.text: / anudbhū[18a3]tāv atra kāle dānapater aparāṇi sāmantakavihāreṇa sārddham /
children.translated_text: When this does not arise — within [that] time, [taking] from the donor's others, together with the neighboring <s>vihāra</s>.
The making of a single receipt of a minor remedy — from the performance of [assigned] work.
When neighboring <s>vihāras</s> are closing — the depositing of property.
When occupied — giving.
They should not give property belonging to one place to another place.
The servant-status of these — when there is no receipt.
Even when there is giving — the non-breaking of the householder's regulation.
In non-giving by force — seizure.
They should give in the manner of a loan.
Property of one place — to another place.

children.text: / nirdoṣam asampattau caityāntare tallābhasya pariṇamanam utsṛjya bodhidharmacakramahāprātihāryadevāvataraṇānām ebhyo 'nyatra /
children.translated_text: No fault — when there is no supply, in the diversion to another shrine-property of gain from that [shrine] — except for the <s>Bodhi</s>[-tree], the Dharma-wheel, the Great Miracle, and the Descent of the Gods — for these, [there is no diversion] to others.
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on diversion. ||29||
The seven-day [rule].

children.text: / vyatītaṃ divasam adhiṣṭhitasya sāptāhikasya bhikṣuṃ śrāyet /
children.translated_text: When the day has passed — of one who has formally authorized [a requisite] for seven days — one should make the <s>bhikṣu</s> hear.
In retention.
Of this.
At the rising of dawn on the eighth [day].

children.text: / [18a5] atyaye 'hne kalpikasyābhyavahāryasya bhuktivad ity atra vyavasthā /
children.translated_text: When the day has passed — of an allowable consumable — the regulation here is as with eating.

children.text: / yasyātrārthe kalpanaṃ taṃ pratyanāpattiḥ kalpitenāsyābhaṅgayoḥ sannihitam /
children.translated_text: For whose purpose here the preparation [is made] — no offense toward him; with the allowable one — non-breaking of both — when [it is] present.

The <s>naiḥsargika</s> on the seven-day [rule]. ||30||
The <s>naiḥsargika</s> [section] is complete.
The <s>prāyaścittika</s> (offenses requiring expiation).
On false speech.

children.text: / saṃjñāya saṃghasannidhāv adharmasya dharmato dharmasya cādharmataḥ paridīpanaṃ sthūlātyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Deliberately, in the presence of the <s>Saṅgha</s> — illuminating the non-<s>dharma</s> as <s>dharma</s>, and the <s>dharma</s> as non-<s>dharma</s> — a gross transgression.

children.text: / kaccit sthā [a]tra pariśuddhā ityā[18b1]tṛtīyapariprasnāt poṣadhe śuddhasaṃjñasya tūṣṇīm bhāvenātināmanāyā duṣkṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'Are you pure here in this matter?' — from the third inquiry at the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day), one who has the perception of purity, by remaining silent — bowing down — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
And in false speech other than the two — <s>pārājika</s> and <s>saṅghāvaśeṣa</s> [offenses already covered].
Even while speaking — when there is the attainment of perception — the arising of this [offense].
One should not take an oath.
The <s>prāyaścittika</s> on false speech. ||1||
Slander.
Of a <s>bhikṣu</s>.
And of the immediately [next in status].
With the desire to disparage or elevate [inappropriately].
By a smooth [person] or by a man.
When speaking [ill] of any person's displeasing conduct.
Even when muteness has not arisen.
Of another's <s>Kṣatriya</s>-status, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-status, and such — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
Repetition [of the slander].
With the intention of slander — when saying 'So-and-so said [this].'
If by name.
And his <s>bhikṣu</s>-status — a <s>duṣkṛta</s> otherwise.
Slander. ||2||
On divisive speech.
