Not [an offense] when [done] for benefit — by the <s>Saṅgha</s> properly.
And when a <s>bhikṣu</s> is the subject of a case — [regarding] divisive speech.
The root [offense applies] only to resident-monks, act-performers, and consent-givers.
Only a <s>duṣkṛta</s> for the view-discloser and the visitor.
Likewise for you — when one knows the matter as a different legal case.
Half [the offense] when one involved in the result of the act conducts oneself without truthfulness.
Cutting off [offense]. ||3||
Teaching.
In teaching.
Of the <s>Dharma</s>.
Beyond the sixth syllable.
For one who knows — in the state of being above [five].
From the fifth, in the commencement of a five-syllable [verse].
Not in cases of: a learned person's successive questioning in the <s>Vinaya</s>, recitation-study, [Dharma-]inquiry-study, question-study, <s>upavāsa</s> (observance), giving, honorarium-teachings.
The non-completion of the prior [offense] when in a different location.
Teaching [offense]. ||4||
Recitation.

children.text: / samam anupasampannena hīnaṃ vā netrībhūtasyoccāraṇe dharmsyākṣarasyāpi /
children.translated_text: Together with an un-fully-ordained person — or less — the recitation of even a letter of the <s>Dharma</s> by one who has become a leader.
Having abandoned, for the impossibility of that [occurring].
Teaching recitation.
And the recitation-study, the repetition-study, and the inquiry-study.
Recitation [offense]. ||5||
Corruption of families.
They should consider [a pair of] wicked monks and nuns — the one who makes families turn away.

children.text: / śṛṇvantvāyuṣmanto kuleṣu kuladūṣakā āśrameṣv āśramadūṣakās tadyathā sampanne śālikṣetre 'śanirvicakrā nipated yāvad eva tasyaiva śāler utsādāya vināśāyānayena vyasanāya saṃpanne vā ikṣukṣetre mañjiṣṭhi[19a1]kā nāma rogajātir niyate[d] yāvad eva tasyaivekṣor utsādāya vināśāyānayena vyasanāya mā yūyam āyuṣmanto 'nena bhikṣunānayā bhikṣuṇyā śāsanaṃ pramiṇuta eṣa bhikṣur eṣā ca bhikṣuṇī dagdhena dhānā aprarohaṇadharmā asmin dharmavinaye bhagavantaṃ paśyata sthavirasthavirāṃś ca bhikṣūn śniti kuleṣu kulapratisaṃvedako brūyāt /
children.translated_text: 'Let the venerable ones listen! In families they are corrupters of families; in hermitages they are corrupters of hermitages. Just as, if a thunderbolt or discus were to fall upon a thriving rice-field, it would serve only for the destruction, devastation, and ruin of that very rice; or just as, in a thriving sugarcane-field, a disease called <s>mañjiṣṭhikā</s> (madder-blight) would enter only for the destruction, devastation, and ruin of that very sugarcane — do not, venerable ones, destroy the dispensation (<s>śāsana</s>) through this monk or this nun! This monk and this nun are like burnt grain — incapable of sprouting. In this <s>Dharma-Vinaya</s>, look to the Blessed One and to the senior monks!' — thus the family-restorer should speak in the families.
When [the accused] does not submit — they should make a formal announcement (<s>jñapti</s>).
Corruption of families [offense]. ||6||
On the announcement of a grave offense.
When the hearer is not provided for, or is un-fully-ordained.
The announcement [applies to both] the <s>pārājika</s> and <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> [offenses].
Not done by one who is not authorized.
When the <s>Saṃgha</s> has not been announced to.
Announcement of grave offenses. ||7||
On the claim of superhuman <s>dharma</s>.
When it is true.
When one who has not seen the truth — not fully ordained.
One should not display psychic powers in front of a householder.
A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> [should not display psychic powers] of the Teacher.
Claim of superhuman <s>dharma</s>. ||8||
On admonishment.

children.text: / [19a3] sthairyeṇa ced artho jñaptipūrvakam arthaṃ kuryuḥ /
children.translated_text: If the matter [requires] firmness, they should perform the act preceded by a formal announcement.
Of one to whom respect has been given.

children.text: / pudgalabhikṣusaṃghābhaktalābhasya mithyāpariṇāmakatvena bhikṣor anyatrāpy anāmnā coktau /
children.translated_text: When a monk, through false transformation of gain [meant for] an individual, a monk, or the <s>Saṃgha</s> — is spoken of elsewhere also, without [proper] designation.
When the content is untrue.
The <s>prāyaścittika</s> of admonishment. ||9||
Wrangling.
When a statement becomes the ground for inattention while [the <s>Vinaya</s>]-related is being spoken.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> regarding the <s>sūtras</s>.
Wrangling [offense]. ||10||
On cutting [a tree] that has not ceased [to be inhabited by a deity].
The construction-supervisor should cut a tree for the purpose of a <s>stūpa</s> or the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

children.text: / prāka tataḥ saptāṣṭeṣu divaseṣv atas tasya maṇḍalakagandhapuṣpadīpadhūpabalidānatridaṇḍakaṃ bhāṣaṇadakṣiṇadeśanāṃ kṛtvā yā devatā 'smin vṛkṣe 'dhyuṣitā sā 'nyad bhavanaṃ samanveṣatvanena vṛkṣeṇa stūpasya saṃghasyeti-karaṇīyaṃ bhaviṣyatīty uktā jānīhi vādena /
children.translated_text: Before that, during seven or eight days, having performed for it the offering of a <s>maṇḍala</s>-circle, incense, flowers, lamp, fragrant incense, food-offering, three sticks, a speech, a dakṣiṇā (honorarium), and a teaching — [one should say:] 'Whatever deity dwells in this tree — let it seek another abode. By this tree, work will be done for a <s>stūpa</s> or for the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' — Having declared this by speech, let it be known.

children.text: / vikāraś ced agnimokṣarudhirasyandanaśākhākampanapatraśaṭanādir udṛśyeta pakṣe 'tra [19a5] dānamātsaryayoḥ saṃvarṇanivivarṇanaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: If a sign of disturbance is seen — such as fire-release, blood-flowing, shaking of branches, shedding of leaves, etc. — during the period, one should praise and criticize giving and miserliness respectively.
Cutting [a tree with a deity] that has not departed. ||11||
On the destruction of seed-sprouts.
When not destroyed [already].
Of both the unprepared seed and the sprout.
In the destruction of <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver grass) and such.
In whatever manner.
Even by shaking.
Even by pressing down — with grass, vegetation, dust, and the like.
Even by excretion and such.
Even by placing in wind and heat.
Even on dry ground.
By one's own will, or by another.
Destroyed — of root-plants; of those destroyed in immeasurable [numbers].
From a lump [of soil with seeds].
In the effort of <s>duṣkṛtas</s>.
The division of this [offense is] at each strike — not by the speaker.
The finality [of the offense is] even when sprouting has occurred — until release.
The existence [of the offense applies] when uprooting water-moss and thorny plants.
The blind swallowing of stone and bone — by the act [of preparation].

children.text: / sādhu syād yady ayaṃ chidyetety uktor niyuktiḥ /
children.translated_text: The commission [arises from saying:] 'It would be good if this were cut!'
The non-causal character of psychic power [for this offense].
The likeness [applies] when the seed is known as another type of seed.
Of bark, pith, yellowish-leaves, flowering, flowered, ripe-fruited [plants] — the practice is [to regard them] as half-alive.
Not of what is not separated from their nature — of the root-element.
Of the half-born, the sown one without a sprouted root — [these have] seed-and-grain [status].
Of small herbs, parasol-shaped, <s>kācikā</s>, creepers, robe-[material plants] and other flowers — by virtue of being half-emerged.
No offense in heating, <s>pūṣa</s>-preparation, walking-path [clearing], pulling of branches and such, <s>maṇḍala</s>-[making] — when there is awareness and that intention.

children.text: / chedane ca kuśāder āpadyavabadhena tenāsambhave mokṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in cutting <s>kuśa</s> grass and such — by confinement [with a wall] — when that is not possible, release [from the offense].
And therefore by one [act], when [the destruction is] multiple.
There is no causal character [of the offense] for what is not of seed-nature.

children.text: / saṃsparśo 'gninā kṣatiḥ śastranakhaśūkhairmlānyutpāṭana utdalanabhiducchittir iti kalpāḥ /
children.translated_text: Contact with fire, cutting with a weapon or nail, withering by [pulling] roots, uprooting, splitting, breaking, and severing — these are the preparations (<s>kalpas</s>).
When it has reached the state of being non-seed — there is no dependence on preparation.
And steam is not non-fire in this context.

children.text: / [19b4] samyamktvasaṃkhyām agninā kalpane phalānāṃ kalpane samudāyarūpasya tantrīkaraṇam /
children.translated_text: The making authoritative of the aggregate form — in counting and preparing by fire, and in the preparation of fruits.
The arising of the possibility of an aggregate from a single portion — not [by assembly].
The completion of the preparations — the monk's duty.
And of the ground, when it is unprepared.

children.text: / nānabhikṣitaṃ śītena vāriṇā sāptāhikaṃ yāvaj jīvakam abhyavaharet /
children.translated_text: What has not been prepared by a non-monk — one should not consume with cold water the seven-day [medicine] up to the lifetime [medicine].
The daily [food] is not affected by this.
Destruction of seed-sprouts. ||12||
On expulsion.
The agency of twelve persons.
Even of the unauthorized.
And of those whose effort has subsided.

children.text: / avadhyāne vā svagatenārthena saśrutaṃ kṣepe vā paravyapadeśena /
children.translated_text: In inattention — or [when one] having heard with one's own [ears] the matter — or in throwing blame — by ascribing to another.
The root [offense is] counted.
Elsewhere, [it is] a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
One should not set in motion one who is unable — even the feeble [person] — for the forbearing [of an act].

children.text: / na svayam enaṃ dveṣyaḥ karmaṇi yujjīta /
children.translated_text: One who is hateful should not himself employ that one in the act.
Expulsion [offense]. ||13||
On obstruction of a command.
They should not disregard: the censurer, the commander, the silent-obstruction-speaker, the individual-facing-detainer, the blame-ascriber-to-another, and the expeller.
By announcement.
In the obstruction of a monk's command.
By that one's consent.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> by another's speech [or] by silence.
And [by saying:] 'I do not remember.'
Unless there is suffering to be declared.

children.text: / tasmād vadhyadarśanaparipraśne viyapa tāvat pānīyaṃtāvat piba viśrāmya tāvan na paśyāmi [20a2] na khaṃ vā paramārthataḥ sattvaṃ napaśyāmi vadhyaś cet yuktāv anāpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the questioning at a place of execution: 'Depart! Drink water for now! Rest for now! I do not see — nor indeed the sky. In the ultimate sense, I do not see a being. And if the condemned one is [truly] yoked [to the act] — no offense.'

children.text: / na yatra sākṣitvena karaṇam āpatet tatrāvasthānaṃ bhajeta /
children.translated_text: One should not assume a position where one would be required to act as a witness.
One should not give a blameworthy [person permission] without having performed an investigation and a closing of the door.
Obstruction of a command. ||14||
On bedding and lodging.
A bed, a bench, a chair, a cushion, a bolster, a four-cornered [mat] — this is bedding and lodging.
Forty-nine <s>vyāmas</s> is its adjacent area.
From the door-chamber, when enclosed.

children.text: / tad atikra[20a3]māya vismṛtyāpi prasthānam antaś ca svapnasamāpatyādinā viparokṣībhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Beyond that — even going out through forgetfulness, and becoming invisible within through sleep, <s>samāpatti</s> (meditative attainment), and such.
The effort [of the offense arises] before the encounter.
In the encounter — the transgression and the completion.
These [acts of] doing and causing to be done do not [apply] to the door.
Not when the monk has been looked at [i.e., informed]; not for one who has reached a difficulty.
The use [of bedding] is like that of a maker.

children.text: / dvayor ekatra niṣāde paścād utthāyinaḥ karaṇīyavattā /
children.translated_text: When two sit at one place — the duty-status [belongs to] the one who rises later.
When simultaneous — [to] the novice.
When of equal [seniority] — to both.
The shameless, the interposed, the elderly, the sick, and the un-fully-ordained — these need not be looked after in this context.

children.text: / eṣa vihāraḥ paśya cedaṃ śayanāsaṃ gṛhāṇa cāpāvaraṇīdānam ity avalokanāni /
children.translated_text: 'This is the monastery! See this bedding! Take it!' and 'Here is the door-screen!' — these are the inspections.

children.text: / saṃbhedās trayo vātena parivarttanaṃ vṛṣṭyā puṭāntaraprāpti[ḥ] dīpikābhiś ca /
children.translated_text: Three [types of] encounter: turning by wind, reaching another panel by rain, and by lamps.

children.text: / śayanāsanatvaṃ sāṃghikatā tasya svayaṃniyuktakṛtatopanikṣepasyābhyavakāśa iti kartṛṇi /
children.translated_text: The bedding-and-lodging character — communal property — of what has been deposited by the self-appointed performer in the open space — [the duty is] upon the performer.
The root [offense arises] at the completion.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> at the effort.
This [applies] only for as much time as is occupied by another in the interval.
And for personal [property].
And in the further four.
Not when in the state of untouchability.

children.text: / piṇḍāya cet praviṣajyāpraviṣṭe vātavarṣam āgacched vihārasthāḥ praveśayeyuḥ /
children.translated_text: If, when one has gone out for alms but not entered [the house], wind and rain come — the monastery-dwellers should let [him] enter.
Having brought [the bedding], one should come when [the other] has entered.
No fault or reduction when this is the purpose.

children.text: / vismṛtya ced bahusamatikrāntādhvano gato vā smṛtiṃ labheta na bhūya evaṃ kariṣyāmīti cittam utpā[20b1]dayed vācaṃ ca bhāṣeta /
children.translated_text: If, having forgotten and gone past much of the road, one obtains remembrance — one should generate the thought 'I shall never do this again' and speak the words.
If one encounters a monk on the way back — one should approach him, and with cordiality, make a request of him.

children.text: / kartṛtvaṃ prāptatāyām atra yena pratijñātaṃ prakramiṣannāvasād asaṃkaṭaprāpto 'bhisaṃkṣipet śayanāsanam /
children.translated_text: The duty-status [arises] at attainment — here, for the one by whom it was agreed upon: the one about to depart, when the dwelling is not in difficulty, should fold up the bedding.
Having beaten it, if soiled.
One should hand it over.
The inspection should indeed be done by another monk.
In his absence, by a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>.
And in the latter's absence, by a householder.
In the complete absence [of all], having looked in the four directions, having secured the door-screen, one should depart.

children.text: / antaramārge ced bhikṣuṃ paśyet taṃ pradeśam asmai brūyāt /
children.translated_text: If one sees a monk on the way — one should tell him the location.

children.text: / dvāre ced antargṛhopanimantraṇāyāṃ badha āgacchet kuḍyasya mūle vṛkṣasya vā nidhāyādhvani praviśet /
children.translated_text: If at the door, when an invitation to enter the inner house [comes], a hindrance arises — having deposited [the bedding] at the base of a wall or a tree, one should enter the road.
They should give seats there.
They should not bring [the seats] themselves.
A householder [should do this] for <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> — this is [the rule].
And in the absence [of a householder], having inspected, the coming to fetch a householder.

children.text: / sthāpayeyuḥ gacchan vayam āneṣyāma iti bruvatsu /
children.translated_text: They should deposit [it], saying 'Go! We shall bring [it].'
When not brought by those who have the support-duties — [they should] bring [it].
In the absence [of supporters] — by oneself.
In all cases — having struck the gong.
They should give [it] at the monastery.
From the invitation-makers — seats at the time of requesting for one's own purpose.
A monk should be stationed for their protection.

children.text: / ekānte 'sau tiṣṭhet svakarma kurva[20b4]nn avadhānadānañ ca /
children.translated_text: That one should stand apart, doing his own work and giving attention.
Entry [is permitted] when [the guests] have departed.
The cleaning of soiled [items] with <s>vakkasa</s>-water.
With oil-bathing for the oily.
With impure clay-<s>oṣāṭuka</s> or with cow-dung.
Airing of the impure [items] in wind.
One who has been invited and seated [by a householder] — the admitted status of the one thus entered.
If elderly or sick — [the duty falls on] the custodian.
The announcing-status of that [custodian].
Everyone should look after the sick.
By sitting with [them].
One should not take the seat there and leave.
The attendant of the sick should provide seats there.

children.text: / kuśalapakṣāpagacchaty ācāryopādhyāye na ca ced anyathā vṛddhiḥ kuśalapakṣasya pṛṣṭhato gacchet /
children.translated_text: When the teacher or preceptor departs from the side of wholesome [qualities] — and if there is no growth of the wholesome side otherwise — one should go behind.
One should personally bring a seat for him.
Not without asking about [his] destination.
One should indeed bring this [seat] oneself.
In the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s> in the open air — the entry of wind and rain into the sleeping-place.

children.text: // svayam aśakto gurutayā vṛttānāṃ navakaiḥ saha parivṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: // When unable himself due to age — exchange with juniors among those who have been trained.
They should station [him] together with a companion.

children.text: / dadyur vihārāntare yācyamānaṃ śayanāsanaṃ vastrañ ca /
children.translated_text: They should give the sleeping-place and cloth being requested to another monastery.
Not when there is rain or the apprehension of rain.

children.text: / vātavarṣa n ced antarmārge syād vṛkṣasya mūle kuḍyasya vā sthalaṃ kuryuḥ /
children.translated_text: If wind and rain [should arise] on an interior path — they should make a place at the root of a tree or of a wall.
And they should cover [the bedding] with a single lower cloth.
Having taken [the bedding] to the monastery — the drying of the cloths.
When burned or carried away — the removal even of <s>Saṃgha</s> [property].
In the event [of fire/flood] — the removal of one's own bowl and robe.
For the protection of what has been removed, they should station a <s>bhikṣu</s> who is least capable.

When there is no assistance — they should enter. //
The <s>prāyaścittika</s> on sleeping-places //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,16) On mattresses.

children.text: // kṛtaṃ saṃstaram antargṛhe ..c chorayeyur avalokya gṛhapatiṃ*
children.translated_text: A made mattress [left] inside the room — they should remove it, having looked to the householder.
Or they should dismantle it in the forest.

children.text: / kṛtatvam asya śironte pādānte vā kṛtatve /
children.translated_text: Its being 'made' — when it has been made at the head-end or the foot-end.
Even for drying robes — grass that has been designated has the character of [requiring] removal.
One seeks a gift [of grass] promised for removal.
They should designate grasses on walking-paths that have been rubbed or [are at] ground level.
Even of those — the character of [requiring] removal.
At relinquishment — the removal of what is to be removed; the non-necessity of doing [it for] what has not come [to that state].

children.text: / anyadā kālena kālaṃ pratyevekṣaṇaṃ parivartanañ ca /
children.translated_text: At other times — periodic inspection and turning over.
In oily and sweet soil — daily.
Elsewhere — not fortnightly.

children.text: / avabadhya ra[21a4]jvā vṛkṣe valalambya caṃkrame(yu)ṣu kakṣapiṇḍakānāṃ sthāpanaṃ /
children.translated_text: [21a4] Having bound with a rope and suspended from a tree — the placing of bundles [of grass] on walking-paths.
One should place cow-dung in a container.

children.text: / prāg gataṃ prāk prakramiṣyanty asmāt tulyatvaṃ sāhyopabhoge /
children.translated_text: 'Previously gone; previously will depart from this' — equal status in the use of assistance.
And of those owners — the observability when non-<s>Saṃgha</s> [property].
The <s>Saṃgha</s>-monastery character — [consisting of] gravel, sand, lime, and such — its own-making nature; therein,
the suitability of a needle and such — of the ground, of a self-appointed maker of a mattress, [with]

a cutter //
The <s>prāyaścittika</s> on mattresses //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,17) On the monastery.
[21a5] The agency [belongs] to [both] being a <s>bhikṣu</s> and [the monastery being] a <s>Saṃgha</s>-monastery.
Not when there is no desire to pacify the arising of crowding, agitation of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and birth [of conflict].
And by another, and following another [monk's initiative].
Of trainees (<s>śikṣamāṇā</s>), male novices (<s>śrāmaṇera</s>), and female novices (<s>śrāmaṇerikā</s>) — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
And of these [female ones].
And in jest.
Of householders — much demerit.
Ejection. // Completed.
// When there has been occupation.
By a <s>bhikṣu</s> — of a <s>Saṃgha</s>-monastery place.
[21b1] Having entered by force — excluding [cases of] sickness, fear, and subjugation — [constitutes] occupation.
This is an example of harassing a <s>bhikṣu</s> with the desire to harass.
Having entered by force — [constitutes] a fall [from discipline]. //
The character of the upper floor of a <s>Saṃgha</s>-monastery — [belongs to] the agent.
Not when there is the character of maturation [i.e., structural change] or the state of [having] boards and such covering.
The character of having peg-feet — of what is not to be stepped upon.
Excluding [what is on] its back [i.e., upside down].
And the character of what has been given [should be] returned.
When stepped upon // Completed.
[21b2] The removable legged[-seat] etc. //
// For one's own enjoyment, from there to elsewhere.
Use together with sentient beings //
// One should procure door-chambers and their giving.
And of bolts.
The opening of windows.
The agency of [building] the monastery.
The measure of the four [areas] of deportment.

children.text: / na cet sarvatvena śailaḥ pakvaśailo dārumayo vā /
children.translated_text: Not when it is entirely of stone, baked stone, or wood.
And covering with water-protection.
'I see it made and completed' — thus, when not spoken by the donor.
Beyond three [courses] — in procuring the giving of successive bricks.
And by another.
On that [same] day.
Elsewhere too — except from mud.
When not released — of water-carriers.
Or when not given — of the base-foot of the foundation.
Or of the upper door-chamber.

children.text:
/ nirdoṣam ādyāt pūrvaṃ /
vihāraprāyaś cittikaḥ // / vṛta
children.translated_text:
Freedom from fault — from the first, beforehand.
The <s>prāyaścittika</s> on the monastery // Completed.
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,18) On instruction [of <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>] by one not authorized.

children.text: // aparājitaṃ sūtraṃvinayamātṛkādharam a[21b4]nunaviṃ*śativarṣaṃ nāgaralapitam upanāmitakāyatve bhikṣuṇyā kṛtapratikriyāṃ bhikṣuṇyavavādakaṃ saṃmanyeran* /
children.translated_text: They should authorize as instructor of <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> one who is: undefeated [in debate], a bearer of <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Mātṛkā</s>, not less than twenty years [of ordination], not given to village-talk, with a body that is properly composed — [and] a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who has performed the remedial act.
On the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance), the fifteenth [day], within the boundary.
In the absence of a bearer of <s>Sūtra</s> and the rest — one who has the current <s>Prātimokṣa</s>.
Even for him — the declaration of the <s>pārājika</s> [offenses].
The eight fundamental precepts (<s>gurudharmas</s>) [should be taught].
'Is there any final [question], O sisters?'

children.text: / samagro bhikṣuṇīsaṃghaḥ pariśuddhasamaveto navadyo mā [21b5]vaḥ kaścid asaṃmata<<ḥ>> saṃghena pudgalo vavadate saṃghād va āgacchati pudgalo vavādako na vaḥ kaścid utsahate bhikṣur avavadituṃ saṃghād vo vavādānuśāsanī apramādena bhaginyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The complete <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>-<s>Saṃgha</s> has assembled in purity. Let there be no reproach among you. No one unauthorized by the <s>Saṃgha</s> [may] instruct. No person comes from the <s>Saṃgha</s> as instructor. No <s>bhikṣu</s> is able to instruct you. From the <s>Saṃgha</s>, your instruction and admonition — with diligence, O sisters!'
'You should accomplish this' — thus, of this [instruction].
Excluding one who possesses the power of higher <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: / ekenāpi vinā tassa<<asa>>mmatasya ca bhikṣuṇya[va]vādena pūrvaṃ sammata..syāsammatatvaṃ /
children.translated_text: Even without one [qualification] — the unauthorized status of one who was previously authorized, by the instruction of <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> by one unauthorized.
Freedom from fault — when the <s>Saṃgha</s> is not full [in number] — of a worthy one — in the request.

And of that [request]. //
Instruction by one not authorized // Completed.
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,19) On instruction after sunset.
When [the sun] has set.
Excluding all-night <s>Dharma</s>-hearing — in the instruction of <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>.

children.text: / na ced apāvṛtadvāras tadā tatbhūtasyāgrato vihārasya varṣakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not when the door is open — then, for one who is of that nature [i.e., authorized], before the monastery in the rainy season.
Instruction after sunset //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,20) On instruction for the sake of material trifles.
For the purpose of fluency in the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s> — a <s>bhikṣu</s> should not bring material [gifts] from a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>.
Of sweets, cakes, balls, and <s>urūcikā</s>s (savory items).
The <s>bhikṣu</s> should take [them only] at first.

children.text:
/ bhikṣor atathābhūtasyāmiṣakiñcitakahetor bhikṣuṇīr avavadatīti vivāde //
āmiṣakiñcitkāvavādaḥ // vṛta
children.translated_text:
When a <s>bhikṣu</s> who is not of that [qualified] nature instructs <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> for the sake of material trifles — [this constitutes] a dispute. //
Instruction for material trifles // Completed.
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,21) Making robes [for <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>].
// When she is not a relative — of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>.

In the sewing of a robe. //
Making robes // Completed.
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,22) On giving robes.
// When given.
When not [in the form of] giving a bolt of cloth.

children.text:
/ na cet* mūṣitāyai saubhāṣiṇikasyopasaṃpadyamānāyai pari[22a3]vartakena vā //
cīvarapradānaṃ //
children.translated_text:
Not when [given] to one who has been robbed, as a friendly [gift], to one who is to be fully ordained, or by means of exchange. //
Giving robes //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,23) On traveling by boat with <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>.
They should carry provisions.
By male attendants, female attendants, male novices, and female novices.
It is proper for <s>bhikṣus</s> and <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> to carry each other's provisions.
And mutual receiving [of provisions].
Not [for] a sick [person].
They should provide shelter for a co-celibate on the road.
They should carry him.
Likewise, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>.
They should render mutual assistance in this matter.
By grasping the head-end.
No fault in proceeding for those who have reached the village.
Having collected food and medicine for the sick through alms-rounds.
Having stationed one attendant of similar [status].

children.text: / muktvo sabhayatāyāṃ mārgasyaikasārthapālam abhinnaprayāṇatāyām ekabhikṣuṇyāpi mārgātivāhane/
children.translated_text: Excluding [times of] danger on the road — with a single caravan-guard and uninterrupted travel — even a single <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> may traverse the road.
Per <s>krośa</s>.
Half a <s>duṣkṛta</s> per each half of that. //
Boat-travel accompanied by <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> //

children.text: // [22a5]sāntarāyatāyām ubhayakulasyocchṛjyā sambidhau yugapad ekanāvā tiryakpārasaṃtaraṇād anyatra /
children.translated_text: [22a5] When there is danger to both families — having relinquished the arrangement — simultaneously, in a single boat, [traveling] across to the other bank — except [when going] crosswise.

And due to the force of a <s>vaṅka</s> (curve), a whirlpool, a turning, an avoidance, a helm-pole, a staff, a bamboo-pole, a breaking, or a helmsman — when boarding for that purpose, from an intermediate departure. //
Boat-travel with <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,24) On [sitting in] one place.
The unfit [nature] of a woman alone with a man — due to the character of a place where people do not pass.
The shared character — within bow-range — thus, of the agent.
[22b1] In sitting.
This is the establishment [of the rule] regarding sitting-down.
At a single sitting-spot.

At a <s>bhikṣuṇī's</s> place. //
One place // Completed.
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,25) On consuming [food] prepared [by <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>].
When cooked by a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>.
With unreal qualities.
When no invitation has been made.
And when it has been made — of the excess.
Of what is to be consumed.
By the success of conduct.
Or by hearing about that.
In consuming — through the throat — this [rule applies].
The character of diminishment — of what is for another's sake.
[22b2] And when [a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>] says 'Give!' when one has entered for alms. //
// Consuming [food] prepared [by <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>] //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,26) On successive meals.
One should accept an invitation to a meal even inside a house.
Having known the time, they should enter — not during the wrong time.
Having sounded the gong.
One should observe one's own assembly there.
An elder [should attend to] newcomers.
One should not suddenly break the meal.
Those requesting a drink should stand.
Equally or afterward — [the reception of] a second invitation [when one has] not obtained the robe-acquisition.
By means of food [that constitutes] a meal.
When it is included within the five [types of staple food].
If another [meal is offered] by this very [means].
Of one who is not sick, who has not done the [assigned] work, who has not been carried on the road.
In acceptance — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
In consumption — the root [offense].
The robe [constituting the] limit — from equally nearby [monasteries].
On the road — half a <s>yojana</s>.
Elsewhere too.
Or in this [matter] — or in not coming [to the meal].
Sweeping — [an area equal to] a mat; smearing — [an area equal to] a small basket — this is the [required] work.
The <s>Saṃgha</s>-nature and <s>stūpa</s>-nature — and of this [property].
The measure of [what constitutes] inability — is sickness.
The non-invitation character of a designation.
And of a display.
The non-existence of what is done [merely] to harass.
Of <s>Saṃgha</s> [property] and that which is not designated for him — and in deposit, and elsewhere among the five [types].
The <s>Dharma</s>-nature of this.

children.text: / grahaṇe py anyasya svīkaraṇaṃ duḥbhikṣo [22b5]āvat saṃpattinimantraṇakānāṃ /
children.translated_text: In taking, the accepting of another's [share] — even in famine — until [the fulfillment of] invitations.
And eating.
And giving.

children.text:
/ a<<na>>bhirucisaṃbhāvane dātur dvitrigrāsābhyavahārād ūrdhaṃ gṛhapate yaṃ bhikṣuḥ piṇḍakena vihanyate numodambā<<svā>>smai dadāmīty abhirocya //
paraṃparabhojanaṃ //
children.translated_text:
When [a donor] estimates [there is] no [further] desire — after the <s>bhikṣu</s> has consumed two or three morsels of what is to be given by the householder — the <s>bhikṣu</s> is refused with alms [and told]: 'We approve! We give to this one!' — having delighted [in that]. //
Successive meals //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,27) On the use of rest-houses.
A rest-house (<s>āvasatha</s>) [is one that] is not of this <s>Dharma</s> [i.e., not Buddhist], has a householder as owner, [and is] for all religious sects.
Of one who is not sick and has not been excluded by the donor. //
Having eaten — the consumption of his [food] — the root [offense].
Of one who has stayed — in staying — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
And [when the place is] without an owner.
The sectarian character here — of one who has gone forth in this [Buddhist] system.

And of one who knows [the rules]. //
The use of rest-houses //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,28) On taking excess [food].
// Of one who is being invited [to stop eating].
Without limit.
Of one who has not been told 'Take as you please.'
By a householder.

children.text: / ardhapañcamānāṃ pakvata[ṇḍu]lamāgadhakaprasthāparimāṇānāṃ [23a2] prasthānām utsṛjya vyañjanam ūrdhaṃ sahāpi sahāyapratyaṃśena piṇḍapātaḥ /
children.translated_text: [23a2] Four-and-a-half <s>prasthas</s> of <s>Māgadha</s>-measure of cooked rice — having set aside the condiment, from above, including the companion's share too — [constitutes] the alms-round [portion].
In having consumed — exceeding [the limit].
Herein — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
And when done by another.
Otherwise — no offense.
And of what is unprocessed.

children.text:
/ grāhyāt prabhūtañ cet bhikṣuṃ saṃvibhajeta //
dvitrapātrapūrātiriktagrahaṇaṃ //
children.translated_text:
If abundant beyond what is acceptable — one should share with a <s>bhikṣu</s>. //
Taking excess of two or three bowls //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,29) On consuming after [being satisfied].
// One should eat until satisfied.
One should not rise with food remaining.

children.text: / yāvatos tā[23a3]vato yasya kasyacid ālavaṇam abhyavahāryasyādāne tadvidhatvaṃ /
children.translated_text: [23a3] In the taking of unsalted consumable food — of however much, of whatever kind — that [offense] character [applies].
Rising from one's place [constitutes] the invitation [to stop].
Of one who is seated.
Of remaining root-food, hard food, and other victuals.

children.text: / mūlagaṇḍapatrapuṣpaphalakhādanīyebhyo nyapaiyāc ca kalpikam asaṃsṛṣ[ṭa]m akalpikenābhyavahāryam abhisaṃbhavanīyapradeśasthasya pratigrāhayato nivāṇaṃ kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: From among root, bulb, leaf, flower, fruit, and hard-food — and what is allowable, unmixed with the non-allowable — [such] consumable food, for one in a proper place [where food] can be estimated, one who causes [another] to accept — having made the invitation [to stop].
'Give!' — this [is the request] of his.
[23a4] 'Go!' — also.
And [having said] 'I have eaten.'
But not yet — when the verbal formulation [is being made].
'It is sufficient' — also [serves as a refusal].

children.text: / sthānasya kalā[c]ikayā ūrdham asaṃpādakatve yavāgvāḥ peyatvaṃ /
children.translated_text: When by the time-mark the proper period has passed — when there is no accomplishment [of the refusal], gruel is [still] drinkable.
Of <s>tarpaṇa</s> (nourishing gruel) — when the five fingers are not discernible [in it, i.e., it is thick].
The non-acceptance of harassment [as a valid mode of refusal].
One should not rise for the purpose of making a refusal to one standing in front — outside the boundary, in places that are to be attended to.
Not [valid] when not in one's own hand — when something needs to be done.
The impropriety of what is not allowable, or of what is mixed with it.
The agency [of offense] — of a place that has not been released.
Even when one who has [already] made the [refusal] resolve — regarding non-eating.
Of what has been requested.

children.text: / gaccha tavaiva bhavatv iti vacanaṃ karaṇam* /
children.translated_text: 'Go — let it be yours' — this statement constitutes the [refusal] act.
'Enjoy as you wish' — according to some.
Having consumed two or three morsels.
One whose [eating] activity has concluded should not partake.
One may eat what has been left over by another who has [properly] completed [his meal].
End of section.
On eating at one sitting.
Of the two [conditions] — having been restrained [from further eating] and not having made a leftover-declaration.
In consumption.

Of food-material only.
Eating at one sitting. [End of section.]
On the appointment of one who has been restrained.

In the appointment — it should be of a <s>bhikṣu</s>.
The appointment of one who has been restrained. [End of section.]
On group-eating.

children.text: // pratiniyatabhaktāvāsekebhyo nyair antaḥsīmasthair bhikṣubhiḥ saṃghabhūtair asahabhaktatāyāṃ /
children.translated_text: When <s>bhikṣus</s> within the boundary, having become a <s>Saṅgha</s>, [eat] other than designated food and food-offerings — not eating together.
Of one who is together [with others].
By virtue of eating together.
By three or more.
Of <s>bhikṣus</s> — of whatever kind — who have obtained food together with a robe as the second [offering], and of one not yet married.
Except at a great assembly.
Another's — from the food of one who has gone forth bearing another's mark.
In partaking — the question-status also applies to those within the boundary who are present and those who are coming.
Eating — is a half-transgression.
In distributing — even a small [amount].
The single-food-[rule] of any person whatsoever.

children.text: / na gamikāgantukaglānatadupasthāyakopadhivārikād anyo ya[23b3]vanopanvāhārād abhuktatāyāṃ ma? sarvair utkṛṣṭya bhuñjīt* /
children.translated_text: No one other than a traveler, a visitor, a sick person, an attendant of the sick, a guard, [or one who takes] a supplementary meal after a <s>yavana</s> [foreign] meal — should eat communally, having separated, when one has not [yet] eaten.
Group-eating.
On eating at an improper time.
From one's own midday to the end of the day, up to the rising of dawn — is the improper time.
In that [regard] — [end of section].

In the consumption of hard food and soft food.
Eating at an improper time.
On the avoidance of stored [food].

children.text: / pūrvabhakte pratigrāhitaṃ paścāt bhakte tatra yāmātikrāntam iti sannihitaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Stored' means — what has been received at the earlier meal-time and has been kept past the time-period at the later meal-time.
What has been taken up — one should not swallow.
Not [what is] cooked [and] kept overnight within the boundary.
And what has been cooked by a <s>bhikṣu</s>.
Cooking here is — that which [transforms] the raw.
The truth — of [foods] that are not soft — [is established] prior to the boiling of a third portion.
Of soft [foods] — by the transformation of color.
Of liquids — from the second rising [of bubbles].
Not by fire — [is] the rendering allowable; it is not cooking.
Not the fabricated nature dependent on birth — the overnight-ness of a vessel.
Even by being in [a particular] place — the bowl's [state of] being cooked by that ground.
Not by the cook's being connected with it.
Fire does not [render something] a non-bowl.
Not the truth of what has been extracted and removed from it.
The overnight-status of [something within] the area of inspection.
A <s>vyāma</s> (fathom) [in measure].
And above — in the space of what is within consideration.
And of what is inside.
The truth — of what is in another city and above.
Not the overnight-status — when another has been formally authorized.

children.text: / na yāvaj jīvikānām utgṛhītāntaḥpakvabhikṣupakveṣu tatpratiśedhe saṃśitatvaṃ kā[24a1]laṃ prati /
children.translated_text: Not, regarding lifelong [medicines] — in [the case of] what has been taken up, cooked inside, or cooked by a <s>bhikṣu</s> — in their prohibition, the restriction with respect to time.
The half-[status of offense] — for the purified [portion].
Drinks and such — [when placed near] the mouth's impurity.

children.text: / bahirasya gomayena mṛdā vā parighṛṣṭodakena sammārgo nirmādanaṃ /
children.translated_text: The outside of this [vessel] — sweeping with cow-dung or clay, rubbed with water — the washing [constitutes] cleansing.
Inside — two or three rinsings with water as mouthwash.

children.text: / nirmāditatvam āśayato dvitravadhikaṃ dāne visvanato pi pātrasya /
children.translated_text: The cleaned status — from intention, two or three additional [washings] — in giving, even when [the vessel] smells — of the bowl.
No fault — when [the contents are] sparse.
And when there is no wrapping — in contact.
And of what has been washed — three times, with alkaline earth, cow-dung, or clay, whichever — when the greasiness [is removed].
The obligation to remove what has risen [to the surface].
When there is a local wrapping of that very [substance] — the obligation to wash.

children.text: / niḥsnehatāyai snigdhasya ca ghaṭāder gambhīra udake hrade nidhānaṃ /
children.translated_text: For the removal of greasiness from a greasy pot and such — immersion in deep water, in a pool.
Holding [the vessel] for licking by fish, turtles, frogs, crocodiles, or <s>vullaka</s>-creatures.
Even from wood — the attainment of non-greasiness.
In cleansing — the purity of what has been de-greased, with alkaline earth or cow-dung.
The half-status — of salt, alkaline substance, or turbid water that has become [mixed with] salt and such.
And the allowability of everything — at an improper time.
The non-existence — when not doing — of salt and alkaline [preparations'] own function.
Upon the arising of the reflection — of the higher [consideration].
With the fruit of the <s>kaṭaka</s> [clearing-nut] — the attaining of clarity of the water.
With alkaline [substance] — [and] with a ball of barley-flour.
Oiling — for the non-splitting of this [vessel].
Not the sentient-being status of what is unperceived — that has entered into [natural] deposits.
In the case of local contamination — the obligation to remove that very [contamination].
When touched by a beak or crow — of the surrounding [area].

children.text: / na tatsaṃyuktadhārā spṛṣṭau na tasya spṛṣṭatā /
children.translated_text: Not when touched by a stream connected with that — not its being touched.
Not by confusion or by lapse of mindfulness.
Not the storing of what has been displaced by both.
One should bring [it] to the nearest intervening place.
Not [one who has been given food] in exchange; not the 'taken-up' status of what has been received or [merely offered].
One should not bring [it] — the grasping of the connection of one worthy of receiving.
The connected-status — of that one, in the connected-status of an intermediate speaker.
The oneness — of stored, received, and taken-up [foods], of two who are equal, with [the same] restraint, with undivided view.
And by the senior — of the junior.
Like householders — of woman and man, mutually.
Having touched [food] of a <s>śrāmaṇerī</s> (female novice) — from concealment, one likewise incurs fault.
Not the released-status of what is given with reservation.

children.text: / ardhatvaṃ nirapekṣotsṛṣṭasya sāpe[24b1]kṣatāyāṃ tasmān netad yāceta /
children.translated_text: The half-status — of what has been released without reservation, when there is reservation thereafter — therefore one should not request this.
One should not accept [it] knowingly.

children.text: / nākalpikatvaṃ bhāganayane spṛṣṭau nītasya praveśane tadrūpeṣu pratyayeṣu /
children.translated_text: Not the impropriety — when touched [food] has been brought and entered in the calculation of shares — in such kinds of cases.
A conveyance-seat on a cart — is to be avoided.
Even when [the cart is] full.
And when a sick person mounts.
Of the corner — in a boat.
And of a seat — for the purpose of holding that [cargo].

children.text: / sāṃghikauṣadhayoś codvalator ghaṭṭanāpanayanenāgninirvāpaṇena cīvarakarṇakādi[24b2]bhir vā tadānenetyādau prayatanaṃ /
children.translated_text: When both <s>Saṅgha</s>-[property] and medicine are boiling over — the effort [should be made] by striking and removing, or by extinguishing the fire, or with robe-corners and such — in bringing that [to safety] and such.

children.text: / kalpikam asampattau vidher nadīsaṃtāraṇārthaṃ netari ca saṃprāpaṇārtham udgṛhītam abhāve nyasya pathyadanaṃ /
children.translated_text: It is allowable — when there is no supply, for the purpose of crossing a river, the regulation — and for the purpose of conveying it to the ferryman — what has been taken up, in the absence [of an alternative], having set it down — eating it as wholesome.
Encouraging [a donation] — in the absence [of supply], of a carrier or donor.
Carrying [it] oneself — when there is no supply.
And the accomplishment from that very [source] — of what is to be accepted as a gift-exchange.
The eatability of this too — when there is no supply, of another's [food].

children.text: / apratigrāhitasya ca pratigrāhakābhāve 'sya cānyasya vā [24b3] kṛtabhaktacchedasya /
children.translated_text: And of what has not been received — in the absence of a receiver, of this or another's — of one whose meal has been cut short.
On the first day — of a tiger, of a camel.
Of both — on the second [day].
On the third — as much as has been obtained.

children.text: / bhojyatvaṃ phalānām akāle py akṛtakalpānām apy apratigrāhitānāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The eatability of fruits — even at an improper time, even of those not [formally] prepared, and of those not received.
Of one without a meal [i.e., who has no food].
When the intensity of hunger [is great].
And of roots.
And oneself — the dropping and producing, and the status of assistance.
From the well-known [principle] of the <s>uttarakuru</s> (northern continent) — in all cases of unprepared enjoyment and such — when desiring [to partake], meditation [should be practiced first].

children.text: / na karake pānīyaṃ pibet saṃbhave hastanirmādanapatrayoḥ /
children.translated_text: One should not drink water from a pitcher — when there is availability of hand-washing and a bowl.
And when there is no availability — [drink what is] not received [formally].
Not even when it is wet — should one incur that [status of offense].
The threefold [nature] of its lid.
Made of wood, made of stone, or made of clay.
One should keep a pitcher-bowl.
Made of wood or made of stone.
No fault — in the use as a vessel — the non-received status of leaves.
No distinction here — between released and unreleased.
The use — when there is no availability — of unreleased [leaves], having set [them] down.
The avoidance of stored [food]. ||34||
On eating what has been received.

children.text: / bhuñjīta tyaktam āśayato dātrānyapratigrāhakābhāve svayaṃ pratigṛhya /
children.translated_text: One may eat what has been abandoned — from intention, by the giver — in the absence of another receiver, having received [it] oneself.

children.text: / sammukhāntaḥsīmny atisaṃbhavanīye pradeśe vasthite nottānapāṇinā kāye tatsaṃbaddhe codgrahaṇasamarthato 'nupasaṃ[25a1]pannād amanuṣyād api dit*śeyāṅgena tatsaṃ*baṃdhena cotsṛṣṭasya pratīṣṭiḥ pratigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Directly [offered], within the boundary, in a place that is very likely — when standing, not with an upturned palm, at the body or connected with it, and capable of taking up — even from a non-human not [fully] ordained — by the seen limb and its connection, the standing of what has been released — is reception.
In the case of disgust — of the countryside — when a circle [of food] has been placed down and shown, 'Here, deposit [it].'
The oneness of the bowl and its support.

children.text: / gocaraḥ śākhāmarkaṭānāṃ na tatas tān pratyanabhisaṃbhavanīyatvaṃ bhūmeḥ /
children.translated_text: The range of tree-monkeys — not from them, the non-likelihood from the ground.
Not — of fruits, the impropriety of reception-standing by the five [methods of] bench, lap, bowl, and support.
The inspection by the preceptors of these — in silence.
And they should approve a distributor of equal activity.
The distributor-status of a <s>bhikṣu</s> is appropriate — of what has been received.
When distributing pots of ghee, oil, honey, and molasses — one should arrange robes [as coverings], using straw, leaves, and such.
When distributing separately — the making [of portions] for the senior, middle, and junior.
Having separated — the distribution of cleaned mangoes.
For the distributor — the <s>ācārya</s> or <s>upādhyāya</s> should receive.
When not reaching those not [yet] reached — the one in the next position.
When there are many — for as many as can receive without leaving their seat.

children.text: / luṭhitasya śakyatāyāṃ svayam amuktvā sthānaṃ grahītum adhvaṃsaḥ pratigrāhasya /
children.translated_text: Of what has fallen — when there is capability, without leaving one's place, to take it oneself — no destruction of the reception.
And of what has been touched by flies, small insects, and such.
Of what has been released by another <s>bhikṣu</s>.
A mouse — is a destroyer.
Not the reception of a non-receiver — is improper.
Eating what has been received. [End of section.] ||35||
On eating what has not been received.
When not received.
Having set aside water and tooth-stick — of what is to be brought.
In consumption by mouth.
In <s>Uttarakuru</s> [— no offense].

children.text: / pratīṣṭhyad glāno nupasampannena bhojanam abhāva upasaṃpannasya /
children.translated_text: A sick person who cannot stand — may eat with [the help of] one not [fully] ordained, in the absence of one [fully] ordained.
One should feed the one not [fully] ordained.
Eating what has not been received. ||36||
On the solicitation of choice foods.

children.text: / kṣīraṃ dadhi navanītaṃ matsyaṃ māṃsam* vallūrā [25a5] iti praṇītabhojanaṃ /
children.translated_text: Milk, yogurt, butter, fish, meat, and dried meat — these are choice foods.
This [rule's] agency — and when the giver is [from] a non-relative household.
In consumption by one's own solicitation — in the solicitation, and when caused to be made — a <s>duṣkṛta</s> for this.
Of one who is not sick and who has not made the 'as-you-wish' invitation.

children.text: / tasmāl labhamānasyāpi ced anyallūhaṃ praṇītam vā samaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ vā vijñaptiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore — even for one who is receiving — if [one requests] another [food], whether coarse or choice, equal or superior — [that is] solicitation.
The half-status — in this [case], of [requesting] coarse [food].

children.text:
/ yathāsukhapravāraṇatvaṃ bhikṣayādāya nirgatena [25b1] tūṣṇīm*
tiṣṭhataḥ pratikṣipto vā tat kiṃ* yācasa iti / prasnasya
children.translated_text: The 'as-you-wish' invitation [is given] by one who has gone out after taking alms-food, [and] stands silently, or is challenged — [by the question] 'What are you requesting?'
The solicitation of choice foods. ||37||
On the use of [water and such] containing living beings.
What is contained in the <s>vibhaṅga</s>.
In the agency of proceeding and causing to proceed — for the purpose of one's own use. [End of section.]
When there is the state of containing living beings.
Water, ghee, oil, honey, molasses, milk, yogurt, butter, vinegar, whey, buttermilk, fruit, edible substances, and such — of what is to be used.
By [beings that are] visible.
Upon death [of the beings therein].
Enjoyment is for the body [directly]; use is for [the body's] instruments.
Namely: bathing, drinking, discarding the tooth-stick, washing the hands and feet.
For things to be employed — that which is [applied] to implements — is use.
Consumable food, bowl, robe, dwelling, tooth-cleaning, fire, and such — these are the body's instruments.
For them [the supplies include] clay, cow-dung, dye, grass, wood, and the like.

children.text: / teṣu upayogas tadyathā nirmādanaṃ bhāvanaṃ* rañjanaṃ* sekaḥ sam*mārga upalepaḥ /
children.translated_text: The uses among them are: cleaning, moistening, dyeing, sprinkling, sweeping, and plastering.
The preparation of broth, whey, and gruel.
The binding and releasing of the water-channel.
The throwing, pulling, and uprooting of wood and rafts.
Bathing with hair-cloth-rubbing and such — other than a skull-bowl.

children.text: / tenāsya hi riktaprāṇakadhātāv udaka ity api prayogāḥ
children.translated_text: For that reason — even in the vessel containing creatures that has been emptied — with water — these are also the efforts [to observe].
The use of [water with] living beings — that pertaining to the <s>vibhaṅga</s>.
(b) That pertaining to the <s>Kṣudraka</s> and other [texts].
One should maintain a water-straining pole.

The given, the returnable, the vessel with raised [opening], the sky-placed, the one being poured, the fan-water-returnable, the purifying — the non-confusing-purpose, the three-pronged-staffed [strainer] — that is its name.
For the placement of the water from the straining — giving a [basin for] the strainer.
Of sand or of cow-dung.
Or of a holding-vessel.
Of either clay or copper.
The binding of this to the three-pronged staff.
Having grasped [it], fastening [it] in the hole with a string — for the former.
For the latter — with a smooth chain.
The maintaining of it.
The counter-stroke of the frequent-swinging-strainer by shaking.
Straining with little effort.
The maintaining of it.
Of clay or of copper.
A potter's task — this [strainer] in the lower pipes — with an internal opening like a lotus.
The purifying function of a reed-[filter] in these.
One should set up a strainer.
A small basket, a <s>dharma</s>-basket, or a release-cloth.

children.text: / ātyuhāyāṃ kalpikajalasya sam*[26a1]bhāvadāyāñ ca karakakuṇḍikābhyām etat tadvattvaṃ / nānena vinājanapadacārikañ caret /
children.translated_text: For urgent need, when purified water may be available — with a water-pot or <s>kuṇḍikā</s> (flask) — this is the same [procedure]. One should not go on a journey through the countryside without this.
Not together with one who has an intermediate [status, i.e., an expelled monk].

children.text: / tadrūpaś cet pratyayaḥ kṣamayitvā kāryakaraṇe stitvam āstitvaṃ /
children.translated_text: If there is a pretext of that kind — having excused [oneself], the standing or being-present during the performing of a duty.

children.text: / tasmāt tadvattvam atra dāne pratijñāte nyena /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the likeness here is in the giving — when promised by another.
This should not be relied upon during a journey through the countryside, when separated and when giving is not promised.
A journey that does not cause obstruction or intermediate wandering.
The same-nature of five <s>krośas</s> (leagues).

children.text: / na pramīlya gatasya sthāne tadvattvābhāve kāmajaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not [an offense] for one who has gone closing his eyes [in sleep] — when the same-nature [of water] is absent at the place — [the offense] is desire-born.
The non-attainment of same-nature for many by one — up to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
The non-obstruction-causing nature of a swift current.
Following one going along a league — downstream — having examined — by that, the procedure.
If the encounter [with creatures] here is through an interval of water — before that.
The examination of a <s>vyāma</s> (fathom) all around.
Purity of water — its purity — by the eye.
By the natural [eye].
When motionless — the examination of what is without impurity.
When the pot is full.
One should not here make excessive repetition for a long time.
Easy for seeing creatures — with a fine brush.
One should not pour it into a swamp by plunging.
Nor another [type of water].
The falling of creatures [must be prevented].
If in a lamp — covering it by [its own] making.

children.text: / pañjaraṃ vaṃśavi[26a4]dalikānāṃ śuklavastrasya veṣṭim abhrapaṭalena vā tadākhyam /
children.translated_text: A cage of bamboo splits, a wrapping of white cloth, or [a covering] of mica — that is its name.
And a hundred-eyed [perforated cover].
First making a skull-cap or a pierced [cover] from a pot and such.
One should not bind a snake with a hair-noose.
Having made a sound without [startling] noise, one should say: 'O good-faced one! Stand on the path of [my] sight!'

children.text: / asthitāvajapadakena daṇḍena śanaiṣkumbhe kuṇḍake vā prakṣipya chidrāṇi kṛtvā mukhaṃ pidhāya niṣkāsanam /
children.translated_text: When it does not stand — having gently pushed it into a basket or a pot with a stick bearing a <s>japada</s>-leaf, having made holes, having covered the opening — removal.

children.text: / [26a5] asaṃmattau paṭṭikayā loṭhikayā murucikayā vā rajupāśena vā natuke veṣṭitena grīvāyāṃ baddhvā /
children.translated_text: When it does not settle — having bound it at the neck with a strip, a ball [of cloth], a fiber-cord, or a rope-noose wound in a hollow tube.
Even in throwing them — the same procedure.
One should not sweep in a forest-fire.
One should stand [only] at a lair-entrance.
The placing of lice in a hollow tube.
In a hole thereof.
Of bedbugs, on grass.
Or in a cool [place].
The prevention of the release-pot from a prior descent.
Or the descent by means of that very strainer.
The release of the strainer — the method when attached creatures have been removed.
The moistening of dirt.
The drying [to prevent] the non-arrival of moisture.
The usefulness of pressing in both of these.
The procedure [takes place] on the occasion of blameless acquisition, or on the occasion of a communal or individual straining and [water-]flowing.
From before sunrise, the continuation of examination for water and pans.
Having lifted and emptied the foot-washing [basin], one should fill it.
One should set up a vessel with water — another vessel.
The store-keeper's work is connected with that — in communal [property].
There is no inclusion here of giving and taking.
Giving to a householder — as a loan.
Of what has been used — when it has that character.

children.text: / nānena dānapatīnāṃ vihāre deyatvasya noktatā [26b3] navasya bhikṣave niddeyatvena /
children.translated_text: By this — of the donors, the state of being giveable to the monastery — is not stated; [it is] not rejectable as new, for a monk.
The assignment of a cell for the purpose of storage.
The depositing separately of clay and copper vessels.
The provision of drinking water.
Not placing [it] just anywhere.
The construction of a pavilion for that purpose.
On the south-west side of the monastery, from the interior.
The provision of ventilation-windows, brick-paving, water-drain-release, door-construction, and shutters with rings.
And for the placement of the bamboo-strainer.
Placement on wooden shelves.
Or on a brick-stand.
On supports.
One should make a clean drinking-vessel, up to [what is needed for] use.
Clean.
And drinking water should be drinkable.
One should not have it carried with unprepared hands or robes.
The internal cleaning of water-vessels from time to time.

children.text: / gambhīrāṇām uśīrakurvakena patravaibhaṅgukair natrakena vā yaṣṭyām upanibaddhena /
children.translated_text: Of deep [vessels] — with a <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver) and <s>kurvaka</s> (small plant) [brush], or with a leaf-<s>vaibhaṅga</s> [brush], or a cloth bound to a staff.
Not from this — the stickiness of a fleshy application.
And drying.
At that time — for the purpose of destruction, by removal.
The work connected with water — for those who have support-duties.
That pertaining to the <s>Kṣudraka</s> and other [texts] connected with water containing living beings. ||38||
On sitting [with women].
In the event or when facing [them].
In an assembly.
Of a woman and a man.
In household [settings].
When in another's place.
And when fit [for the offense to apply].
When the connected one is dismissed.
In sitting as if in a private-like [manner].
Sitting with [a woman while] eating.
On standing.
Standing in a private-like [manner].
Of one who has a screen.
Not if through compulsion of fear.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> when the knower and the known are not known.
And when attention [is given] at another place.
From the end of the range of vision — being within the place.
The being-inside nature of a thicket.
The separateness of another house.
The place of eating together.
On giving to a naked [ascetic].
To a woman or a man.
Excepting a kinsman, one who wishes to ordain, and a sick person.
To a naked (<s>acelaka</s>) non-Buddhist ascetic who has not ordained with this mark — upon the body or what is connected to the body.
Of hard food and soft food.
One's own and the other's.
Excepting [giving] for the purpose of distinguishing from one gone to wrong views.
In giving by oneself.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> for both who are unprepared.
In causing to give.
And in sharing.
Giving to a naked [ascetic].
On viewing an army.
For the purpose of viewing an army that delights in battle.
Excepting the directive of a king, queen, prince, minister, officer, military-commander, townsman, or countryman.
And [excepting] the force of an intervening calamity.
Of one who has been dispatched.
When the boundary of the adjacent area is transgressed — in viewing.
Viewing an army.
On dwelling with an army.
Permitted [only for] that — beyond the fulfillment of two days and nights of dwelling.
And without cause, even before [the limit].
Dwelling with an army.
On experiencing the accessories of war.
The agency of the accessories of war.
Of one not under the power of an intervening [cause].
Of [weapons] assembled and dispersed.
Of those readied.
The root [offense] of the root.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> in the effort.
Of those not readied.
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> only in both [cases].

children.text: / spṛṣṭir udyūthanaṃ prasthāya darśanārtham upavicārāntātikrame dṛṣṭir iti mūlāni /
children.translated_text: Touching, brandishing, going [to view] for the purpose of seeing, and vision when the boundary of the adjacent area is transgressed — these are the root [offenses].
The reduction [in penalty] when not brandished.
One should not make, cause to be made, or watch elephant-fights, horse-fights, cock-fights, quail-fights, partridge-fights, woman-man fights, and so forth.
Experiencing the accessories of war.
On striking.
With a turbid mind.
With the body, [something] released from it, or connected to it — with anything whatsoever, down to a toe, a mustard-seed, or a brush — when one has struck.
A monk.
Another's.
In the upper three [types of person].
Touched.
A <s>pratinipātya</s> (prostration-offense) [should be performed].
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> when there is no falling [in prostration].
One should not strike elsewhere when one ought to strike somewhere else.
One should not strike a post.

children.text: / na bhittau bhūmyāṃ vṛkṣe nyatra vā /
children.translated_text: Not a wall, the ground, a tree, or elsewhere.
Striking [offense].
On threatening.
Threatening with a strike.
For each weapon.
Threatening.
On concealing a fault.

Of the <s>pārājika</s> and <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> [offenses] — excepting [concealing due to] the force of fear of touch-defilement, harm to the ascetic life, harm to celibacy, disturbance of the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
In concealing.
At the end of a day-and-night.
Before [that] — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
When another's non-offense [is mistakenly identified].
Concealing a fault.
On causing the cutting off of food.

children.text: // saṃ*cintya muktvā rogapratikṛyārtha tāṃ gṛhī dātṛbhaktachedasya kāraṇe /
children.translated_text: Intentionally — except for the purpose of treating disease — when a householder-donor causes the cutting off of food.
Causing the cutting off of food.
On fire-procedure.
One should not touch a lion [i.e., fire as powerful as a lion].

The expectation that [fire] serves the righteous purposes of the Teacher, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and fellow celibates — and for bowl-glazing and dyeing — the determination of the proper time.
One should tend [the fire] for a long time.
And in play, with foot-and-hand [gestures], and from making fire-wheels of the moon, sun, firebrands, and such.
By fire.
When one who has not determined the proper time and is not under the power of illness — touches [fire].
By oneself or by commission.
In kindling, extinguishing, touching, not-touching, covering fuel, proper extracting, coal-banking, and extracting.
The half-extinguished nature of charcoal.
And of flames.
In covering and extracting — therein for fuel — the fire-procedure between.
Of hair, body-hair, bone, nail, phlegm, nasal-mucus, vomit, excrement, <s>mudga</s> (green gram), <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), sesame, oil, honey, and ghee — the half-fuel nature.
When another should perform — 'place this!' — this is the determination; the half-determination.
Fire-procedure.
On the withdrawal of consent.
In an act for a monk's purpose.
For the purpose of withdrawing a cast vote.
Withdrawal of consent.
On sleeping [in certain places].
One should not sleep in a place that does not have the light of the moon or sun, [in] an enclosed room.
Except through the force of being sick or attending upon the sick.
'There is a <s>prāyaścittika</s> here' — some [say].
Half [the offense] from non-occurrence; and the separateness from [the daytime offense of] the day.
What is mostly enclosed — the limit is the house-boundary.
The belonging-to-that of what is connected [to the house] — the adjacent area of the door-side of the house-natured [structure].
And of the interior [of a different house] — of the connected door's adjacent [area].
Not of what is more than the adjacent area — from a mere cell — a separately standing occupied [room].
Half [the offense applies to] tree-roots, wall-cavities, [and other semi-enclosed spaces].
The sleeping <s>prāyaścittika</s>.
On sleeping together with a woman.

children.text: / adhvano tra kukkuṭasyotpātya nilayane ntaram abhūtatvaṃ /
/ akalpini ca bhikṣor karaṇīye tatsaṃpādakena sārdhaṃ* glānasya tadupasthāyinaś ca /
/ śrāmaṇereṇa ca tadvataḥ sannihitatāyāṃ tatrāvāse pāpabhikṣoḥ kṛtakurvattan nivāsaprayatnasya /
/ middhopapātenādhvani śrāmaṇeram abhiplutaṃ* purataḥ kṛtvā gacchet* /
/ bubhukṣitaś cet sānukālaṃ dadyād asmai tadāhāram* /

// tathāham bhagavato dharmadeśitam ājānāmi yathā <<y[e] adharmā[ḥ] saṃkleśikā[ḥ]>> āntareyikadharmā uktā bhagavato pratiṣevyamāne <<nā>>lam antarāyāyetyādi pravṛttavacanatāvasarge jaigupsyamata enaṃ kuryu jñāpanena /

/ jñapte caturthasya te karmaṇa iti pūrvatrottaratranāśanīyasya te ity upakramaṃ jñapti<<ḥ>> kṛtā ni<<ḥ>>sṛjedam evaṃrūpaṃ pāpakaṃ dṛṣṭigataṃ prathamā karmavācanā kṛtā dvitīyeti pratyetadantam asmai bhikṣuṇā śrāvayeyuḥ /
/ ekatve vṛddhāntād ārabhya yāvat saṃbhāvanām uparidānaṃ /
/ śastram etat saṃgrāmāvacaraṃ bhāṇḍañ ca gandharvāvacaraṃ /
/ saptāṣṭān divasanetadupavicāre prakra[29a1] / /ṣyan pāṃsunā vaibhaṅgukair vā chādayeta /
/ nāsamuditacinnāya svāmy aham iti bruvate dadyāt* /
/ ūrdham anāgatau yat bhūmau buddhasāṃghikayor labdhiṃ* tatropayuktiḥ /
/ tadā cet svāmy āgacched anujñānam āyā..ya[29a2]n ichate dadyuḥ /
/ vṛddhiñ cet mṛgayed etad eva na bahu manyase yad asmābhiḥ paripālitam iti brūyuḥ /
/ gopayitvotrāse gṛhītvā vānuparodhe svasya sāṃghikam* [29a4]staupikañ ca hiraṇyasuvarṇam apakramaṇaṃ /
/ nirdoṣam amānuṣabhavane puṇyanirjātaṃ ced eṣāṃ ratnamayaṃ bhūmisopādānādi /
/ atra ca maṇipratyupteṣu suvarṇarūpyakhaciteṣu / praveśayeyur etāni /
nākalpikatvam upasthāpitaśāstṛsaṃjñānām āgārikaśrāmaṇerābhāve buddhapra<<ti>>kṛter dharmyārthavaśatayā spṛṣṭau /
/ cihnaṃ sāṃghikāyām madhye cakraṃ pārśvayor mṛgāv adhastād vihārasvā[29b2]mino nāma(ḥ) /
/ na cet* stambhasya[29b5]śuṣire kuḍyasya vā nikṣepaḥ /
/ śiṣṭād adhyardhato grīsmasya pūrvataś ca varṣāṇāṃ māsāt* /
/ na saṃbhave parasyotsvāsakalpaṃ saṃśrayet snātaprāyaś cittikaṃ //
<</>> tadānyadā vā tannidānaṃ mṛtau duṣkṛta(kṛ)tvaṃ satvāvigrabhasya /
// na tvam upasaṃpannaḥ parājayikam asyāpanna ityādyartha bhikṣvarthena kaukṛtyopasaṃhṛtau [30a5]bhikṣoḥ /

children.translated_text: // Of a <s>bhikṣu</s>.
By touching with the finger, fist, forearm, shoulder, head, side, back, hip, thigh, calf, knee, foot, big toe, and such — with the intention of shaking [the other].
Therefore, from seeing a wound, blemish, wart, mole, or hair-whorl and so forth — an offense [arises].
Some [say] — when one or many are to be admonished.
The <s>prāyaścittika</s> on poking //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,64) On water-play.
// In the performance of activity in the domain of water.

Of one who has entered [the water] — diving, surfacing, crossing from one bank to another, swimming against the current, water-exercises, water-drum-playing, water-ball-playing, the swinging-game, piercing, circling, diamond-[dive], well-[dive], whirlpool-making, drawing lines on the water — [all of these constitute] the root [offense].
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> — for taking a ladle [for play].
In a round pot, a water-vessel, or a basin.
[30b2] And in broth, soup, or gruel — even when it is heated.
And in non-water play.
Likewise — the cause of that being of that [playful] nature.
With the desire for experiencing excitement and passion.
Therefore — no offense when entering [water] and the like with the desire for refreshment.
In learning to swim — or in crosswise long [exercise].
With the desire to amuse — drawing lines on hot [surfaces].
Water-play //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,65) On sharing a bed with a woman.
// Sleeping — together with a woman — overcome by drowsiness — at night — in a single room.
At the end [of the rule].
Beforehand — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
This is the hen-measure — having done [it] — at the end.
Sharing a bed with a woman //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,66) On frightening.
Even in jest or viewing — with the desire to frighten, through the prior presentation of signs of fear — in the informing.

children.text: / bhayaṃkarasyāmuko yam iti bhikṣoḥ pareṇāpy anutpattāv api bhayasya /
children.translated_text: 'This one is frightening — such-and-such one is this' — of a <s>bhikṣu</s>, by another too — even when fear has not arisen.
The root [offense] — when the mind is [indeed] afflicted.

children.text: / tad yathā pretapiśācakumbhāṇḍakaṭapūtanatvā[30b4]khyāpinām* kīṭanaṃ kīṭakīṭānām aṅgārikā<<varṇā>>nāṃ dagdhasthūṇānibhānāṃ rūpāṇāṃ /
children.translated_text: Namely — by the appearance of forms resembling ghosts (<s>preta</s>), goblins (<s>piśāca</s>), barrel-spirits (<s>kumbhāṇḍa</s>), evil spirits (<s>kaṭapūtana</s>) — by insects resembling insect-insects — by forms resembling embers — by [appearances] resembling burnt pillars.
By sounds of a lion, tiger, leopard, owl, and <s>rubhraṣṭoroka</s>.
By smells of excrement, urine, and cadaver-stench.
By the touch of thorns, straw-dust, and heated [objects].
A <s>duṣkṛta</s> — when the mind is [merely] afflicted.
Namely — by the appearance of those proclaiming themselves as gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, or <s>mahoragas</s>.
[30b5] By forms of wealthy men, guild-chiefs, caravan-leaders, and the like.
By sounds of the <s>vīṇā</s> and such.
By fragrances of <s>aguru</s> (aloewood), sandalwood, saffron, and <s>tamāla</s>-leaf.
By the touch of silk, fine cloth, shawl, muslin, and cotton.
The purpose of generating spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>) [is valid].

Therefore — no offense for the purpose of generating urgency — in narrating tales of hells, animal births, hungry ghosts, and human [suffering] and such. //
Frightening //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,67) On hiding.

This [refers to] the hiding of items belonging to a renunciant's livelihood — bowl, robe, water-strainer, <s>kaṃsikā</s> (bell-metal vessel), [31a1] body-band, and other requisites of a renunciant's life.
And in causing [them] to be hidden.
The purpose of wishing to benefit having been relinquished [i.e., with mischievous intent].
Hiding //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,68) On living off what has been given [to another].

children.text: // dattasya bhikṣor nirdeyaṃ cīvarasya vinā tadanujñānaṃ paribhoge /
children.translated_text: // Of a robe given to a <s>bhikṣu</s> that should be given away — in enjoying [it] without that [owner's] permission.

children.text: / na ced asya tannidānaṃ prītes sambhāvanā /
children.translated_text: Not when there is the estimation of affection arising from that [previous giving].
Living off what has been given //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,69) On false accusation.
// With the desire to destroy — informing a <s>bhikṣu</s> of a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> or <s>pātanīya</s> offense while having the perception of 'destroying.'
[31a2] Even partially.
The <s>prāyaścittika</s> on false accusation.
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,70) On traveling with a woman.
Willfully, when traveling on a road.
Per <s>krośa</s>.
Half of that — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
Having abandoned — one who is causing excessive delay.
If she is lost — bringing [her] down from the road.
Or of one who is unable to be carried.
Traveling with a woman //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,71) On traveling with thieves.
// With village-plunderers, robbers, tax-evading merchants.
With deceivers and those who have ordained through theft — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
[31a3] Traveling with thieves // Completed.
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,72) On ordaining one under [twenty] years.
When the one to be ordained is under twenty years of age.
In ordaining as a preceptor.
He should not ask him about his completeness [of age].
Nor should others.
They should not ordain him without ascertaining.
In all cases — full ordination [is valid only] from the completion of twenty years — that is the established rule.
When the other has the perception of being complete.
And in [cases of] doubt — 'I am not,' 'I am,' or uncertain.
And [31a4] when there is knowledge — the destruction [of the ordination].
Not when it has reached completion.
Even together with the months in the womb.
Ordaining one under [twenty] //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,73) On digging the ground.
// Of digging and causing to dig.
Of living earth.
Excluding the digging of a mere four-finger peg — of a building overseer — by stellar [i.e., astrological] procedure — of an attendant not present.
If [the earth is] living — the root [offense].
If not — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
That which has been lying for three months without consolidation — is the former [i.e., dead earth].
[31a5] If [there is] an interval of rain.
Six [months] — otherwise.
One should not think 'it is not [living]' regarding a blanket [of earth].
In assemblages — the efficacy of signs [determines living or dead earth] by predominance.

children.text: / tasmāt kārtsnyam eva sa nyūnānyatra vṛtāyāṃ /
children.translated_text: Therefore — completeness [of the offense applies] when less [than the full amount], elsewhere, when it is completed.
When it has perished or been burned.
The half-status of what has perished.
And of split [earth-surfaces] — of earth-flakes, embankments, walls, floor-plastering.
Or when gravel, sand, and such are predominant.
And of the acts.

[31b1] The uprooting of pegs, drawing lines, scratching, pulling out earth-granules, pulling out cow-dung, shaking mud, uprooting balls adhering [to surfaces], removing salt-deposits — [these are] of that nature.
Without the intention of concealing — this [rule applies] here.
Therefore — no offense for the intention of counting, placing, and the like.
Digging the ground //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,74) On excessively attending upon one who has invited [one to stop eating].
// One should not beg excessively.
It is proper — when the time has not been announced, when there is no estimation of that [sufficiency] — to approach the food-offering house.
[31b2] And urging — in serving, when the time falls [due].
One should not treat the matter of a fan as if it were [the offense].
One should accept each individual invitation [to stop].
Even when the <s>Saṃgha</s> has [collectively] been invited [to stop].
And at all times.

children.text: / vinā maryādāvyavasthāpanena pravāritavato nyathā paunaḥpuṇyenātyarthatayā cordham akṛtapravāraṇāca<<t*>> caturthamāsaparisamāpter ūrdhaṃ prajñaptābhyavahṛtau /
children.translated_text: Without the establishment of a boundary-convention — of one who has been invited [to stop], otherwise, through repetition, through excessiveness, and from the non-performance of the invitation [to stop], from the completion of the fourth month onward — in the consumption of what has been designated.
In the solicitation — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
[31b3] No offense — in sickness.
And when known.
The separateness of the former [offense] — due to confusion.
The character of causing the fault of [eating as if] not invited [to stop] — is his.
Even beforehand — by whomever he has not been invited [to stop].
Excessively attending upon one who has invited [one to stop] // Completed.
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,75) On rejecting the withdrawal of training.
When recognized.
Of the one who declares.
In the training.

children.text: / asyānte śikṣitasya mityākhyā dayamānāyām uddeśena vā bhikṣuṇā na śi[31b4]kṣiṣyāmīty etat kāraṇabhāvena nivedayiturajñatām utbhāvayato vacanasyodāhṛtau /
children.translated_text: At the end of this — when the one who has been trained is being falsely declared — or by designation — when a <s>bhikṣu</s> [says] 'I will not train' — in the statement of [31b4] one who presents this as a cause, exhibiting ignorance of what is to be announced.
In the sūtra-context — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
Rejecting the withdrawal of training //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,76) On eavesdropping.
Of a <s>bhikṣu</s>'s deliberation of a case — listening in by <s>bhikṣus</s> — the purpose having been relinquished, with the desire for pacification — in paying attention.
In perceiving the sound — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
Of the meaning — the root [offense].
If [done] with the inclination of causing disturbance.

children.text: / arthāntara[31b5]vaśāyām upaśliṣṭau cetanād ūrdham padacchaṭotkāśanaśabdādibhiḥr acetayato na cet mugdhaḥ śamārthī vā niyatamātṛtāyāṃ pātaḥ /
children.translated_text: [31b5] When [one is] adhering [to the wall] in subjection to another purpose — from awareness onward — by sounds of footsteps, sneezing, coughing, and such — of one who is not aware — if one is not foolish or desirous of peace — in the certainty of the motive — a fall [into the offense].
One should not foment a quarrel.
One should not eavesdrop; one should not stand downwind of one who is doing [such deliberation].
One should not [refrain from] making effort for pacification.
Eavesdropping //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,77) On breaking the harmony [of the assembly].
// Having assembled for a formal act beginning with a motion (<s>jñapti</s>), departing without looking at [i.e., notifying] a <s>bhikṣu</s>.
In exceeding the hearing-inspection — the root [offense].
Beforehand — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
Without a proper reason — in departing.
When the motion has been performed.
And when the act is improper.
When there is no desire to exceed the hearing-area — no offense.
Breaking the harmony //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,78) On disrespectful conduct.

Of what has been presented regarding standing, going, bedding, dwelling-place, acquisition, speaking, and its opposite — through disregard of its purpose — except [when done] by the giving of a proper designation — in transgression.
By the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>Saṃgha</s> — the root [offense].
By the <s>ācārya</s> or <s>upādhyāya</s> — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
When the motion is improper — the applicability of interrupting the discourse.
'The happiness of the <s>Saṃgha</s>' — is its administrator.
Like the <s>Saṃgha</s> — [so is] the <s>Buddha</s>.
One should not provoke the command of the king, <s>Arhat</s>s, <s>Saṃgha</s>, or elders.
Disrespectful conduct //
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,79) On drinking intoxicants.
// In the drinking of an intoxicating [substance].
Its departure from that nature — in a decoction.
It exists in consuming husks and such — [then there is] its entry.
Half-status — for a lump of ferment.

children.text: / madanīyānām mūlagaṇḍapatra(pa)puṣpaphalānāṃ madyagandharasānāṃ vā madayitṝṇāṃ peyānāṃ /
children.translated_text: Of roots, bulbs, leaves, flowers, and fruits that are intoxicating — or those having the smell and taste of liquor — those that intoxicate — [and are] drinkable.
Freedom from fault — [when] merely resembling liquor in color.
Like the attempt — holding a mouthful [of liquor for medicinal purposes] and anointing the body.
An offense — from sickness.
Drinking intoxicants // Completed.
(<s>Vin</s> 2,4,80) On going about at the wrong time.
In the wrong time [i.e., after noon].
Of a <s>bhikṣu</s> who has not notified a co-resident.
In entering a village.
Not when there is a gathering for an extremely urgent matter.
In wandering elsewhere — a <s>duṣkṛta</s>.
In the absence of a <s>bhikṣu</s> — likewise, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>.
For her — a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>.
For him — a <s>śikṣamāṇā</s> (probationary nun).
For her — a <s>śrāmaṇerī</s> (female novice).
Non-applicability — for one who does not understand.
And of those suspended, those in another boundary, and those of another party.
